Which Hamilton schools and historic districts matter to buyers?

Hamilton City Schools serve most of the city, and Hamilton High School is the main public high school. Small pieces of the city fall in the Talawanda and Ross Local districts, so confirm the district for your street. Badin High School is the Catholic choice, and Miami University Hamilton, open since 1968, enrolls more than 5,000 students.

  • Dayton Lane, German Village and Rossville are the city's three historic districts and hold much of the oldest housing.
  • Exterior changes in a historic district or to a listed property need a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Architectural Design Review Board.
  • Bus routes from the Butler County Regional Transit Authority link to Middletown, Oxford and Springdale.

If your house is in one of those districts, tell buyers early, because planned exterior work will go through that review.

How is Hamilton governed, and who handles city services?

Hamilton uses a council-manager form, adopted in 1926. Seven council members are elected on a nonpartisan basis to staggered four-year terms, they choose a mayor from among themselves, and together they appoint a professional city manager to run daily operations. The city employs more than 675 permanent staff and reports a budget above $400 million.

The public safety department covers police and fire, with more than 110 full-time officers and more than 110 full-time firefighters. The city's Vital Statistics office issues certified birth and death certificates for $25 per copy, which can matter when an estate needs paperwork to settle a house.

What do Hamilton's permit, vacancy and rental rules require?

Hamilton's Building Department takes permit applications at building@hamilton-oh.gov and answers questions at (513) 785-7360. The Planning Department, at 513-785-7350, handles zoning, conditional use and variance questions. Electric, plumbing, HVAC, gas and sewer jobs call for a registered contractor.

The permits page also describes an annual vacant building registration with a fee that rises each year, aimed at commercial and industrial buildings. If your empty house might fall under it, ask the city before you list.

Chapter 758 of the city code governs stays under 30 days. A host needs a license before operating or advertising.

  • Owner-occupied accessory rentals offer up to two bedrooms with no fee. Large and commercial rentals pay $50.
  • Licenses last two years and renewal is due 30 days ahead.
  • An emergency contact must respond within 24 hours, and utilities must be current.
  • Enforcement climbs from a letter to a $250 fine, then $500 and a six-month suspension, then revocation and a fine up to $1,000 per day.

The city's permits page links each application.

When can a Hamilton seller skip Ohio's disclosure form?

Many Hamilton sales come out of estates and rentals, so the carve-outs in R.C. 5302.30 come up often. Executors, guardians and trustees selling for others are exempt, and so is an heir who inherited the house and never lived in it during the past year. Court-ordered sales, foreclosure sales and deeds in lieu of foreclosure are exempt too.

An investor who bought a rental and never lived in it fits none of those categories, so tenants in the house do not change the duty to provide the form. The statute lists each category.

How does the Butler County Auditor process a Hamilton deed?

The Auditor's Conveyance Department handles every ownership change in Butler County and collects the fees. The real estate conveyance fee is $.30 per $100 of price, which equals $3 per $1,000, and the price is rounded up to the next $100. A $0.50 charge applies to each parcel.

  • Only cash or a check payable to the Butler County Auditor is accepted.
  • Staff cannot make change or fill in a blank check.
  • For residential rental property, the Auditor's endorsement notes that the buyer must file landlord information under R.C. 5323.02.

The deed transfer page has the forms. Your title company usually delivers the deed.

When does a quick cash sale suit a Hamilton owner?

It suits a house that needs more work than the price supports, a property with tenants, or an estate on a deadline. Set a written cash offer beside the net you would keep from a repaired listing after repair bills, commissions and months of carrying costs.

More questions about Hamilton, OH

Do I need a permit to run a vacation rental in Hamilton?

Yes. The city requires a Short-Term Rental License before you operate or advertise stays under 30 days. Accessory rentals of up to two bedrooms pay nothing, and large or commercial operations pay $50.

How is the Butler County deed fee figured?

Take the sale price, round it up to the next $100, and charge $.30 per $100, which is $3 per $1,000. Add $0.50 per parcel. Pay by cash or a check made out to the Butler County Auditor.

Does an inherited Hamilton house need the state condition form?

Often it does not. R.C. 5302.30 exempts estate fiduciaries and heirs who did not live in the house during the prior year. A title agent can confirm your case.

Which school district covers my Hamilton street?

Most addresses are in Hamilton City Schools, but some sit in Talawanda or Ross Local. Ask the district to check your address.

Do historic district rules limit what a Hamilton buyer can change?

They can. Outside changes inside a historic district need Certificate of Appropriateness approval from the Architectural Design Review Board, and the city lists Dayton Lane, German Village and Rossville.

What is it like to sell a house in Youngstown, Ohio?

Youngstown, the Mahoning County seat, is the largest of the four Ohio cities compared here, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate counts 58,832 residents. That is down 2.0% from the April 2020 estimates base of 60,049 and well below the 66,982 counted in 2010. Selling here means working with a market shaped by the steel era, a smaller population than the city was built for, and a lot of older housing.

The city grew around coal, iron and then steel mills along the Mahoning River. Wikipedia notes that local ore ran out early in the twentieth century and that mills had to bring ore in by rail, which put Youngstown at a cost disadvantage and started its manufacturing decline earlier than in some other cities. The effects are still visible in the housing stock and the tax base.

Youngstown became the county seat in 1876, when the seat moved from Canfield. The county auditor's offices, the courthouse and most of the records you need for a sale are in the city.

How do Youngstown home values and incomes compare?

Prices are a different scale from the other cities in the table. QuickFacts puts the 2020 to 2024 median home value at $63,300 and median rent at $728, with 56.2% of the city's 24,982 households owning. Median household income is $34,408, and 37.3% of residents are in poverty.

  • Monthly owner costs run $916 with a mortgage and $379 without, the lowest of the four cities.
  • The city is 41.4% White alone and 40.4% Black alone, with 12.3% Hispanic or Latino residents.
  • The largest employer in the city is Youngstown State University, which serves about 11,000 students.

Health care is the largest of the sectors QuickFacts lists: about $1.32 billion in 2022 receipts for health care and social assistance, compared with $418.5 million in retail sales. Youngstown's other major employers include Vallourec Star Steel in Brier Hill and Trivium Packaging.

Which Youngstown neighborhoods do buyers and investors ask about?

Wikipedia divides the city into downtown, a North Side, a South Side and other districts. Downtown holds government buildings, banks and venues such as the Covelli Centre and Powers Auditorium, with Youngstown State University and the Butler Institute of American Art just to the north. The North Side includes Brier Hill, Crandall Park, North Heights and Wick Park, where industrial executives built mansions that still stand in historic districts. Brier Hill hosts a festival at the end of every August.

The South Side is the densest and most populous part of the city and includes Oak Hill, Erie, Warren and Lower Gibson. Interstate 680 serves the city directly and connects to I-80, the Ohio Turnpike and State Route 11. State Route 711 runs north, and the Madison Avenue and Himrod Avenue expressways form a freeway loop around downtown.

The Youngstown City School District covers almost all of the city and has been under state oversight since 2015. Wikipedia reports that the graduation rate rose from 65% in 2015 to 88% in 2020. Catholic and private schools within the city include Cardinal Mooney High School and Ursuline High School.

What must a Youngstown landlord or owner register with the city?

Registration is the Youngstown rule that surprises sellers most. Under Section 546.11 of the city's Codified Ordinances, every rental property must be registered and licensed annually, other than public housing and Section 8 units, which follow federal inspection rules. The city's Property Code Enforcement and Demolition page adds that, except for owner-occupied homes, all properties must now be registered.

  • The fee is $40 for a single rental unit. In a multi-unit building it is $40 for the first unit and $25 for each additional unit.
  • An unlicensed rental can be fined $100 for each week it is unlicensed, and criminal penalties are possible.
  • Once the form and fee arrive, a provisional license is issued for one year while an inspection is scheduled within 30 days.
  • If the property fails inspection the owner has 30 days to fix the violations, and each re-inspection costs $40.
  • Cancelling an inspection after 8:00 a.m. on the day costs $25, and later late cancellations cost $100 each.

Vacant properties have their own registration program run by the same office. Before you list a vacant house, call the Property Registration Department at (330) 742-8743 and ask whether the address is registered and whether fees are open. The office keeps weekday hours from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

Can a Youngstown house on the demolition list still be sold?

Ask the city first, because Youngstown decides which houses are condemned. The Mahoning County Land Bank says it works at the request of cities, villages and townships when demolition funds are available, and that local governments decide which houses are condemned. In Youngstown, call the Property Code Enforcement and Demolition office at (330) 742-8888 to ask where an address stands.

The Land Bank also answers several questions that come up in sales. It keeps no list of houses it owns and says it had no houses in inventory to renovate. It does not hold owner phone numbers, so a buyer must find the deeded owner through the auditor's property search. It also says the idea of buying a house for $1 is an urban legend.

If a house is torn down, taxes still follow the building for a time. The Mahoning County Auditor says taxes are collected a year behind, so you are still taxed on the building's value if it was standing on January 1 of the tax year being collected. A demolition permit for a Youngstown residence comes from the city's Property Code Enforcement and Demolition Department.

How does Mahoning County set values, and when can you appeal?

Ohio requires each county auditor to reappraise every parcel every six years. Mahoning County completed its reappraisal for tax year 2023, with taxes collected in 2024, and the next reappraisal is for tax year 2030. A triennial update, which studies sales without visiting each property, applies to tax year 2026 with taxes collected in 2027.

Owners who think the county's number is high file a Complaint Against the Valuation of Real Property, accepted from January 2 through March 31. Three officers sit on the Board of Revision, the auditor, the treasurer and the commissioners' president, and the hearing covers value only. Its address is 120 Market Street in Youngstown, and the auditor's office can be reached at (330) 740-2010. For payment questions, call the county treasurer at (330) 740-2460.

What the Mahoning Board of Revision accepts for residential value complaints
EvidenceDetail printed by the auditor
Recent saleClosing statement, purchase agreement and conveyance statement for a sale within 24 months, with a notarized arm's-length affidavit
ListingA listing agreement if the property is currently for sale
AppraisalA report by a certified appraiser for tax valuation, subject to review
ConditionPhotographs with professional repair estimates
New constructionBuilder-certified costs for work five years old or less

The auditor adds that tax increases themselves are not a ground for a value complaint, because taxes result from voted levies.

What does Ohio require a Youngstown seller to disclose?

The state disclosure form under Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 covers most one to four unit sales, with carve-outs for foreclosure sales, deeds in lieu, court-ordered transfers and estate fiduciaries. Anyone selling in one of those roles should confirm which carve-out applies.

The city also publishes a Property Transfer Affidavit, listed among the forms on its code enforcement page. Ask the Property Code Enforcement and Demolition office whether your sale needs one before you set a closing.

When does a cash offer make sense for a Youngstown house?

A cash offer makes sense when the cost of repair, a rental license problem or a vacant-property registration issue would hold up a conventional buyer's financing. A lender's appraiser and inspector will look closely at a house with roof, plumbing or foundation problems, and the low median values here leave little cushion.

Compare more than one offer, ask who pays closing costs, and get the closing date in writing. Request the settlement statement early and check that any unpaid city fees or taxes come out of your proceeds.

More questions about Youngstown, OH

Do I have to register a rental before I sell a Youngstown house?

If the house is rented, the city says it must be registered and licensed annually, and an unlicensed rental can be fined $100 for each week. Call the Property Registration Department at (330) 742-8743 to confirm the status of your address before closing.

What if my Youngstown house is vacant and on the demolition list?

Call the Property Code Enforcement and Demolition office at (330) 742-8888. The Mahoning County Land Bank says local governments decide which houses are condemned and that it acts on their requests when funding is available.

When do I file a value complaint in Mahoning County?

File between January 2 and March 31. The auditor's page says complaints for tax year 2026 begin January 2, 2027, and mail or in-person filing goes to the Board of Revision at 120 Market Street.

Is there a disclosure exemption for estate sales in Youngstown?

Yes. The disclosure statute excuses an estate fiduciary, and it also excuses transfers made by court order.

Will I still pay tax on a Youngstown house I demolish?

Yes for the year in question. The county auditor explains that taxes are collected a year behind, so a building standing on the January 1 tax date is still taxed that year.

What is the Springfield, Ohio housing market like for a seller?

Springfield is a lower-priced, renter-heavy market, and that shapes who buys a house here. The 2020 to 2024 American Community Survey numbers in QuickFacts put a typical owned home at $116,800 and typical rent at $851. Owners hold 52.4% of the 24,650 households, and the median household earns $47,143.

The city is the seat of Clark County, about 45 miles west of Columbus and 25 miles northeast of Dayton, on the Mad River, Buck Creek and Beaver Creek. Counts fell from 60,608 in 2010 to 58,662 in 2020, and the latest federal estimate, for July 2025, is 58,281 residents over 25.97 square miles of land. Many buyers are investors planning to rent, so expect offers built around rental income and repair cost.

How did Springfield's industrial past shape its houses?

Many older houses date from the factory years, when Springfield called itself the Champion City. Wikipedia says the National Road reached Springfield in 1838, that manufacturing flourished through the mid and late 1800s and that International Harvester and Crowell-Collier Publishing were the largest local employers for much of the twentieth century.

The city's population peaked above 82,000 in the 1960 census. Since then the loss of manufacturing jobs left many neighborhoods with aging frame houses, a point that matters when you price a house and decide how much repair to put into it. The city also has pockets of historic architecture, including the South Fountain Avenue Historic District and the Frank Lloyd Wright-designed Westcott House on East High Street, and houses near them can draw a different type of buyer.

Does Springfield require landlords to register rental property?

Yes. The city runs a Rental Property Registry, and the city says rentals make up nearly half of all households. A landlord with a tenant in place should confirm the registration is current and the annual fee is paid before listing.

  • Single unit property: $35 each year
  • Two or more units in one building: $25 per unit each year
  • Cap of $750 per owner and per LLC

The city says the self-inspection checklist is not currently required to finish a rental registration. Questions go to 937-324-7385, and registration is done through the city's online portal, City Works Online. A buyer may ask for proof of registration, so keep the receipt with your closing papers.

What is the vacant property registry in Springfield?

Springfield also keeps a Vacant Property Registry, which it administers through HERA Property Registry. If your house sits empty, ask the city's Responsible Property Programming office whether it must be registered and what the registry charges.

The office is at 76 E. High Street on the second floor, with City Hall's posted hours running from 8 in the morning to 5 in the afternoon Code complaints against an empty house can follow it into a sale, since boarded windows, tall grass or failed systems tend to show up in a buyer's inspection. Owners of empty houses often weigh an as-is sale for that reason.

Which schools, roads and colleges matter to Springfield buyers?

Most addresses fall in Springfield City Schools. Wikipedia counts 14 schools and about 7,000 students: ten elementary, three middle and one high school, with one alternative school besides. Parts of the north are in the Northeastern and Northwestern local districts, and parts of the west, south and southeast are in the Clark-Shawnee Local district. Check which district a specific address falls in before you advertise it.

Downtown is crossed by State Route 72 (north to south) and U.S. 40 (east to west). U.S. 68 skirts the west side and Interstate 70 passes to the south. Wittenberg University, founded in 1845, and Clark State College supply a steady stream of renters near campus. The average commute is 21.2 minutes.

What local amenities help a Springfield listing?

Outdoor access is the easiest selling point to document. Buck Creek State Park and the Clarence J. Brown Reservoir sit on the city's northeastern edge, and the paved Little Miami Scenic Trail, nearly 80 miles long, starts at the Buck Creek Scenic Trail head in Springfield and runs south to Newtown.

  • Wittenberg University has a 114-acre campus and about 1,300 full-time students, which supports demand for rentals and small houses nearby.
  • Clark State College adds a second source of student and staff tenants.
  • Downtown has seen new construction since 2000, including a regional medical center and a surgical hospital, which keeps hospital jobs close to the central neighborhoods.

Photos of the trailhead, a short drive to campus or a quick route to I-70 can matter more than a long feature list, especially when the buyer is an investor comparing several rentals.

What do Clark County tax dates mean for a Springfield closing?

The county collects in two installments. For the 2025 tax year, the first fell due February 27, 2026 and the second August 7, 2026. Penalties start the day after: a 5% penalty on the unpaid half from February 28 to March 9, rising to 10% on March 10, with the same two-step pattern for the second half in August.

Bills are mailed 20 to 25 days ahead, and a bill that never arrives does not waive the penalty. The Treasurer's office, 937-521-1832, can give the balance on your parcel. The county also runs an escrow program for monthly prepayments. Your title agent will prorate the bill by days of ownership at the closing table, so ask to see that number early.

What do Ohio recording rules require for a Springfield deed?

Under R.C. 5301.25 a deed is recorded in the county where the land lies. Before the auditor indorses it, the grantee files a statement of value (R.C. 319.202), and the grantor pays the conveyance fee. When the property is a residential rental, the indorsement also reminds the grantee to file landlord details with the auditor, which affects investor buyers.

Is a cash sale the right fit for a Springfield house?

It can be, if repairs would eat the gain from a retail listing. With a median value of $116,800, one big job such as a roof or furnace weighs heavily against the price, and a financed buyer may insist you do it first.

A direct buyer typically purchases as-is, which suits a vacant or tenant-occupied house with open code items. Get two written offers, ask who covers closing costs, and review the settlement statement before the closing date.

More questions about Springfield, OH

Is there a city inspection before a Springfield house can be sold?

Ask the city's Responsible Property Programming office at 76 E. High Street whether your address has open code items or a vacant registration. Springfield's rental and vacant registries are the main property rules that touch a sale.

How much does Springfield charge to register a rental?

The annual fee is $35 for a single unit and $25 per unit in a building with two or more units, capped at $750 per owner and per LLC. Call 937-324-7385 with questions.

When was the second half of the 2025 Clark County tax bill due?

It was due August 7, 2026. A 5% penalty applied from August 8 through August 17, and 10% from August 18, according to the county Treasurer.

Who pays the conveyance fee on a Springfield sale?

Under R.C. 319.202 the seller pays the fee, plus any county transfer tax the county has levied. The title company can quote the exact amount.

Which Springfield neighborhoods are historic?

Wikipedia names the South Fountain Avenue Historic District, and the Westcott House on East High Street was designed by Frank Lloyd Wright. Check with the city before planning exterior changes on a historic street.

A Kettering owner who wants top dollar and has time should list with an agent, while an owner facing a deadline, heavy repairs or an estate usually gets further with a cash buyer. Selling alone sits in between, since the commission stays with you along with every task.

  • Listing: the broadest exposure, with the schedule set by buyer financing and the appraisal.
  • Owner sale: lower cost and more legwork, and the buyer is still owed the state property disclosure form.
  • Cash purchase: a quick close on the house as it is, which matters when the roof, furnace or wiring would scare off a lender.

Ownership runs high in Kettering: 64.9 percent of households hold title to the home they live in, and 86.5 percent of residents stayed put over the previous year. Sales here tend to involve long held houses with years of accumulated repairs and records.

How did Kettering's housing stock come about?

Kettering is a young city carved out of farmland. Van Buren Township, created in 1841, gave way to the Village of Kettering after voters approved incorporation in November 1952. The western part seceded in 1953 to become Moraine, and by 1955 the village had 38,118 residents and was proclaimed a city on June 24. It is named for inventor Charles F. Kettering, who lived at Ridgeleigh Terrace from 1914 until 1958.

Postwar migration out of Dayton fed the growth, and the census count peaked at 69,599 in 1970. Numbers then slipped for decades as the population aged and manufacturing jobs left, bottoming at 56,163 in 2010 before the 2020 count rose to 57,862. Wikipedia describes Kettering as the most populous suburb in the Dayton area, covering about 18.7 square miles of land.

A city that filled in during the 1950s and 1960s has plenty of postwar houses, so buyers often ask about wiring, plumbing and windows, and the property maintenance code gives everyone a checklist to use.

How do Kettering's numbers compare with nearby cities?

Census estimates put Kettering at 57,396 people in mid 2025, a dip of less than one percent from 2020. The table sets Kettering beside Lakewood, another large Ohio suburb with a very different housing mix.

What do Kettering's schools, parks and roads mean for a seller?

Kettering is served by the Kettering City School District, which includes Kettering Fairmont High School, eight elementary schools and two middle schools. Private options include Archbishop Alter High School and several parish schools, and Kettering College offers nursing and allied health programs. Use the district name accurately in a listing and point buyers to the district office for attendance questions.

  • Parks and culture: the city counts 20 parks, the Fraze Pavilion concert venue, Rosewood Arts Center and Pondview Park's nature trails.
  • Neighbors: Dayton, Oakwood and Riverside lie to the north, Moraine and West Carrollton to the west, and Centerville and Beavercreek to the south and east.
  • Transit and commute: the Greater Dayton Regional Transit Authority runs buses, and the typical worker spends about 20.3 minutes getting to work.

Kettering has four fire stations, and its police department holds accreditation from two national bodies.

How do Kettering permits and property maintenance rules touch a sale?

Kettering reviews construction through its Planning and Development Department, reachable at 937-296-2441. Under Ordinance 1301, a project needs approval from every city department that applies, whether building, fire, zoning or stormwater, before work starts. The city aims to finish reviews in 10 days and says it can take up to 30 when demand is high.

  • Certificate of Occupancy: issued only after the required inspections pass and every department signs off.
  • Finished work: if you added a deck, finished a basement or replaced a furnace, locate the permit and final inspection record before you list.
  • Rental condition: the city's landlord and tenant guide says an owner must keep mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems up to code, heating able to hold 68 degrees, and water heating at no less than 110 degrees at the taps.

A structure that fails the code can be condemned and posted as unfit for human habitation, so cure visible violations early. A rental seller can also point the buyer to the same guide to show what was maintained.

How is a deed transferred in Montgomery County?

Because Kettering sits in Montgomery County, the County Auditor processes the deed transfer, and the Auditor's page says this step is needed for the transfer to count as a legal transaction. The page lists a conveyance fee of $3 per $1,000 of the actual sale price plus $.50 for each parcel, and gives 937-225-4373 for questions. Filers can also use ePN or Simplifile for electronic submission.

Ohio Revised Code 319.202 requires the buyer's side to file a statement declaring the property's value, and it puts the fee on the seller. A seller who has claimed a property tax reduction should expect to answer a question about it on that statement.

Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 covers the disclosure form for one to four unit homes. It lists exceptions such as transfers by court order, by an executor or other fiduciary, and between spouses or parents and children. Most arm's length sales of a Kettering house do need the form.

Is a cash offer the right call for a Kettering owner?

Take a cash offer when the sale must follow your timetable and the house would struggle in a conventional listing. Examples include a worn mid century home, a property with a code citation still open, or an estate whose heirs live elsewhere.

Get every offer in writing and weigh it against what an agent would likely net after commission, repairs and carrying costs. Settle who pays title and recording fees plus the Montgomery County transfer charge, and keep your own copy of the disclosure form and any permit records for the buyer.

More questions about Kettering, OH

What is the Montgomery County transfer charge on a Kettering sale?

The County Auditor's page lists $3 per $1,000 of the actual sale price plus $.50 per parcel. Under Ohio Revised Code 319.202 the seller bears that charge, and it should show on the settlement statement.

Will a buyer ask for permit records on a Kettering house?

Buyers and lenders sometimes ask for one. Kettering's Planning and Development Department at 937-296-2441 can tell you what was permitted and whether a final inspection was passed.

Can a Kettering house sell with an outdated furnace or wiring?

Yes, a house can sell as is, but the seller still completes the Ohio disclosure form under Revised Code 5302.30 and answers honestly about known problems. Cash buyers price the repair in, while financed buyers may ask the seller to fix it.

Which school district do Kettering addresses belong to?

Most addresses are in the Kettering City School District, whose high school is Kettering Fairmont. City and district boundaries can differ, so a buyer should verify a particular address with the district office.

Who handles property maintenance complaints about a Kettering rental?

The city's Planning and Development Department answers questions about the code at 937-296-2441. The landlord guide on the city site lists the standards for walls, hallways, plumbing, heating and wiring that owners must meet.

Which selling route gets an Elyria house closed quickest?

For most Elyria owners the quickest path is a buyer who pays cash and skips mortgage underwriting. A listing with an agent reaches more people but waits on a lender, and a by-owner sale puts every task on you.

  • Agent listing: best for a tidy house that will show well, with time to wait through appraisal and loan approval.
  • By-owner sale: saves the agent's fee, but you price the house, run showings, hand over the state disclosure form and chase the paperwork.
  • Cash buyer: fits houses with deferred repairs, a tenant, a probate title or a deadline, since the buyer takes the property as it stands.

Lorain County houses built for the factory workforce of the last century often carry old roofs, boilers and wiring. Those items are exactly what a financed buyer's inspector flags, and exactly what a cash buyer prices in up front.

What shaped the Elyria housing market?

Heman Ely built a log house, dam, gristmill and sawmill beside the Black River in 1817, and the village that took his name became the Lorain County seat. By 1900 it held about 8,800 residents, and the 1910 count reached 14,825. Census figures kept climbing until 1980, when the city peaked at 57,538 people. Then the car plant closings of the 1970s and 1980s, plus the opening of Midway Mall in August 1967 on the edge of town, pulled jobs and shoppers away from downtown.

The population slid to 52,656 by 2020, then turned upward: the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 53,634. Voters passed Issue 6 in March 2016, a 0.5 percent income tax increase earmarked for police, parks and fiber internet, after companies such as Bendix and 3M shifted operations elsewhere.

The employer list in the city's 2021 financial report still reads like a county seat: UH Elyria Medical Center with 1,934 jobs, Lorain County government with 1,718, Lorain County Community College with 1,609 and the Elyria City School District with 971. Bendix Commercial Vehicle Systems, Walmart, Ridge Tool, Invacare and Parker Hannifin follow. Many buyers come from those payrolls and want an address within a short drive of work.

Getting around is straightforward. Lorain County Transit is based in the city, the Elyria Amtrak station and Greyhound service sit in town, and Cleveland Hopkins International is the nearest major airport. Cascade Park follows the Black River through a ravine cut by the same glaciers that shaped the Great Lakes, and its East Falls is a local landmark that listings often mention. The Elyria City School District rebuilt Elyria High School, with the new building finished for the 2012 to 2013 school year, which changes how some families view the district.

How do the Census figures describe Elyria homes and households?

Census Bureau QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 put Elyria's median owner occupied home at $156,100, and 60.0 percent of homes are lived in by the people who own them. The 2020 census counted 24,904 housing units, with 7.8 percent of them vacant. The median resident was 40.3 years old, and about 35.5 percent of the 22,954 households held one person living alone. The city covers roughly 20.8 square miles, with 2,562 residents per square mile in 2020.

Small households and a rent level near $906 mean many Elyria buyers are first time purchasers or investors who run the numbers against rental income. A house with a signed lease in place appeals to the second group and can scare off the first.

Which Elyria offices should a seller call before closing?

Start with the Building Department at 131 Court Street, Suite 101, phone 440-326-1491. It issues permits, enforces the Ohio residential code and the city's codified ordinances, and investigates property maintenance complaints. Ask whether any permit on your address is still open, because unfinished work is the item most likely to hold up a closing.

  • West by the River district: exterior repairs, replacements and additions to homes in this historical district need approval from the Landmarks Preservation Commission. Interior changes and gardens do not.
  • Rental registration: the permits page carries a Rental Unit Registration Form. Landlords selling a rental should confirm the registration is current.
  • Accessory structures: sheds, fences and pools use the zoning permit application, and a missing permit can surface in a buyer's inspection.
  • Utilities: the Utilities office at 440-326-1570 sets up water, sewer and sanitation accounts, so tell it about the sale date.
  • Regional income tax: the city homepage links to RITA for filing and paying, which matters if you move out of the city.

What happens to the deed after an Elyria sale?

Because Elyria sits in Lorain County, the Lorain County Auditor, at 226 Middle Avenue, Room 200, phone 440-329-5207, processes the transfer. Its real estate department takes transfers Monday through Thursday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

  • Transfers arrive in person or by approved e-filing. Mailed transfers stopped being accepted on November 1, 2012.
  • The cutoff is 3:00 p.m. for e-filed documents and 4:00 p.m. at the counter.
  • The matching conveyance or exemption form must be typed and complete, since handwritten forms are rejected.
  • Incorrect fees or blank lines mean the packet comes back, and staff keep nothing for later.

Under Ohio Revised Code section 4705.01 the Auditor's staff may not fill in forms or advise on deeds, so a title company or attorney normally prepares them. Separately, Ohio Revised Code section 5302.30 makes owners of one to four unit residential property deliver a signed disclosure form to prospective buyers. The statute lists exceptions, including transfers by an estate fiduciary and sales by an heir who never lived in the home.

When does a cash offer on an Elyria house make sense?

Cash works best when certainty matters more than squeezing out the top price. Typical triggers are a roof near failure, a basement that floods, a tenant who will not leave, a relative's estate, or a lender deadline.

Ask each buyer for a written offer that names the closing date, who pays title and recording charges, and what happens if their walkthrough finds something new. Collect two or three offers and ask for proof of funds. Then ask the Lorain County Auditor's real estate department what conveyance fee applies, so the number on your closing statement holds no surprises.

More questions about Elyria, OH

Is it possible to sell an Elyria house without fixing anything?

Yes, selling as is is a common choice. You still owe buyers the Ohio disclosure form when Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 covers the transfer. Financed buyers may ask for repairs after their inspection, while a cash buyer typically prices the work into the offer.

Who handles code complaints and open permits for an address in Elyria?

The Elyria Building Department, reached at 440-326-1491, handles both. It can tell you whether permits are open and whether complaints are on file for the property.

Which office records the transfer of an Elyria property?

The Lorain County Auditor in Elyria transfers the deed, either in person or through an approved e-filing vendor. Mailed real estate transfers are not accepted.

May I sell Elyria rental property with a tenant living in it?

Yes. A tenant in place does not bar a sale. Read the lease for its end date and notice terms, tell buyers about it early, and confirm your city rental registration is current.

How much is a typical owner occupied home worth in Elyria?

The Census Bureau lists $156,100 as the 2020 to 2024 median for owner occupied homes in Elyria. Condition, street and size move your own number, so compare recent nearby sales.

How does a home sale work in Middletown, Ohio?

The city lies along the Great Miami River, roughly 29 miles northeast of Cincinnati and 20 miles southwest of Dayton, and it straddles two counties. Butler County holds most of it, with a smaller slice in Warren County. Your parcel's county decides which auditor processes the deed and which school district applies.

Census estimates for 2025 show 52,146 residents, up from a 51,004 base in April 2020. With just 54.0% of households owning, a seller may hear from move-in buyers and investors both.

How do Middletown's ownership and rent numbers look?

Renters make up close to half the city, and owned homes have modest values. A mix like that draws investors, who often bid on houses that need work.

At the 2020 census, 8.0% of the city's 23,007 housing units were empty, and about one household in three was a person living alone. Owners of an empty house keep paying taxes, insurance and utilities each month while it waits.

What does Middletown's steel history mean for older houses?

Stephen Vail Jr. platted 52 village lots in 1802 on the river's eastern bank. A canal link to Toledo and Cincinnati opened in 1825, paper and farming drove the early economy, and in 1900 George Verity started a sheet steel plant for the American Rolling Mill Company. That plant still runs as part of Cleveland-Cliffs.

The population climbed from 9,215 in 1900 to 23,584 in 1920 and peaked near 51,605 in 2000. A house from the steel-town growth years may have older wiring, plaster walls and masonry foundations, and those are the items an inspector's report usually turns into a price request. Hook Field Municipal Airport, a Miami University regional campus that opened in 1966, and State Routes 4, 73 and 122 shape daily life, with I-75 just east.

What do schools and transit look like in Middletown?

Anywhere in the Butler County part of Middletown, students belong to the Middletown City School District, which operates Middletown High School. The Warren County part is divided among the Middletown City, Franklin City and Lebanon City districts, so confirm the district for the address before writing a listing.

Buses from the Butler County Regional Transit Authority link to Hamilton, Oxford and Springdale, where riders can switch to the Cincinnati regional system. The median age was 38.0 in the 2020 census, with 23.2% of residents under 18, so families often ask about districts early.

Which Middletown property standards could come up in a sale?

Development Services publishes a maintenance sheet that draws on the International Property Maintenance Code and local ordinances. A buyer's agent or city inspector may point to these items:

  • Grass and weeds: kept under 6 inches, and cut within 5 days of a city notice (Ordinance 678).
  • Junk vehicles: a non-running vehicle left uncovered more than 7 days after notice breaks the rules (Ordinance 660.07).
  • Furniture, mattresses and appliances outside: not allowed in a yard or on an open porch for more than 48 hours (Ordinance 660.21).
  • Windows: broken glass must be repaired, and screens are required on windows.
  • Pools and hot tubs: a pool or spa holding more than 24 inches of water needs a surrounding barrier of at least 48 inches, with a gate that closes and latches itself.
  • Trees: branches must clear 12 feet over the street and 9 feet over the sidewalk.
  • Sidewalks: the owner keeps them in good repair and free of snow, ice and leaves.

Ask Code Enforcement if the address has open notices. A nuisance abatement or unpaid mowing charge is easier to resolve before closing than afterward.

What does a Butler County deed transfer involve?

On the Butler side of Middletown, deeds go through the Butler County Auditor's conveyance desk. Its posted rate is $.30 per hundred dollars of price, restated as $3 per thousand with the price rounded up to the next $100, and $.50 more for each parcel. A transfer never costs less than $3.00 plus the parcel fee.

  • Payment is cash or a check payable to the Butler County Auditor, and staff cannot give change.
  • A valid legal description must be on the deed, and the County Engineer's office should approve it ahead of submission.
  • Submissions may arrive by mail, in person or by e-file with a finished DTE 100 or DTE 100EX.
  • The auditor does not prepare transfer on death affidavits, so that drafting falls to a real estate attorney.

The auditor's records start in 1993, and deed copies sit with the Recorder. A parcel in the Warren County part of town follows Warren County's schedule instead, so ask that auditor for its fees and steps. State law (R.C. 322.02) caps a county transfer tax at thirty cents per hundred dollars.

What did Butler County report about values and tax relief?

The Butler County Auditor's news page carried a June 2026 item stating that residential values were rising 19% countywide and that new legislation would blunt the tax increases. A July 2026 item described an inflation cap credit now applying to second half bills under House Bill 186.

The same office added a tool that shows each levy by taxing district for any parcel. Open the Current Tax Distribution tab on your parcel, and note that the totals there are calculated before rollbacks such as the owner-occupancy credit or homestead exemption, so the figures run higher than your bill. Ask the auditor how a sale in the current year affects credits the next owner can claim.

What if the house was inherited or used as a rental?

Ohio's disclosure statute (R.C. 5302.30) exempts some transfers from the seller form, such as sales by an estate fiduciary and sales by an heir who has not occupied the home for a year. A buyer will still ask about the roof, sewer line and water damage, so answer honestly and in writing.

For a tenant-occupied house, the city's eviction page says landlord and tenant disputes are filed in the civil division of Middletown Municipal Court. It lists a $115 filing fee for one defendant, $20 for each added defendant, and a $15,000 ceiling on damages or counterclaims. An owner that is not an individual needs an attorney. When the deed is endorsed on a residential rental property, the auditor's endorsement reminds the buyer to make the county rental property filing under R.C. 5323.02.

When does a cash offer make sense for a Middletown house?

With a midpoint value near $164,400 and many older houses, repair costs can eat a large part of the sale price. A direct sale can suit a house that needs a roof, a vacant property with code notices, or an estate whose heirs live far away.

Get the terms in writing, learn who pays transfer fees and title costs, and fix the closing date. Then compare the number with a realistic listing net after repairs, commissions and waiting time.

Which county handles my Middletown deed?

That depends on where the parcel sits. Butler County covers most of the city and Warren County a portion. Check the parcel on a county auditor's property search to see who processes the transfer.

What is the Butler County conveyance fee?

Butler County's auditor posts $3 per thousand of price, with the price rounded up to a full hundred, and $.50 per parcel, payable by cash or check.

How high can my grass be in Middletown?

Keep them under 6 inches. After a city notice the owner has 5 days to cut. Confirm current wording with Code Enforcement before you list.

What is Middletown's median home value?

QuickFacts gives $164,400 as the midpoint for owned homes. A particular house can sit far from that, depending on size, age and repair needs.

Can I sell a Middletown house with tenants in it?

Yes. A sale does not cancel a lease on its own, so give the buyer the lease terms and deposit details. Cases that need an eviction go to Middletown Municipal Court.

How does a house sale work in Newark, Ohio?

Newark is the Licking County seat, 40 miles east of Columbus at the junction of the Licking River's forks, and it counts as part of the Columbus metro region. Only 17 Ohio cities are larger. Deeds for a Newark sale go to the Licking County Auditor on South Second Street.

The 2025 estimate of 51,473 residents stands 3.0% above the 49,961 base from April 2020. Growth of that kind supports housing demand, yet buyers still compare condition closely, and roughly 44 of every 100 households rent.

How do Newark's ownership and rent figures compare?

Use these figures as a rough check on any offer, keeping in mind that they describe the entire city and never one block.

Counting housing units in 2020 gave 22,351, of which 6.9% sat vacant, and the vacancy rate for rentals alone was 6.3%.

What is special about Newark's history and economy?

The Hopewell culture built the Newark Earthworks between roughly 100 AD and 500 AD, and the Octagon portion was named part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site in January 2025. The first European-American settlers came in 1802 under General William Schenck, who named the village for his New Jersey hometown. On July 4, 1825, two governors broke ground for the Ohio and Erie Canal at Licking Summit, close to Newark.

Manufacturing has long anchored jobs here. Holophane lighting dates to 1898, Heisey Glass operated from 1895 to 1957, and Owens Corning has a main factory in the city, with industrial parks that house Dow, Boeing, International Paper and others. The Longaberger basket headquarters is the best-known building. Ohio State University at Newark shares its campus with Central Ohio Technical College, and the Newark City School District teaches the city's public school students. Newark High School enrolls about 1,400, and the Licking County Library System runs two branches in town, details a family weighing a move will often check.

What does Newark's weather do to an older house?

Yearly totals in Newark run 43.40 inches of precipitation and 15.2 inches of snow, and records span 106 degrees down to minus 26. The wide swing is hard on gutters, flat roofs, porches and driveways, and the wettest months, May through July, each average more than four inches of rain, which raises the odds of basement moisture.

  • Clear gutters and downspouts and look for water lines on basement walls before showing the house.
  • Check porch posts and concrete steps for freeze damage.
  • Note the age of the furnace, water heater and roof, since inspectors record each one.

Small repairs made early can matter more than fresh paint, because an inspection report hands the buyer a list to negotiate from.

What do Newark buyers see around the house besides the lot?

Buyers weigh commute options and nearby landmarks. Licking County Regional Airport is about 3.5 miles southwest of downtown, Licking County Transit offers demand-response and deviated fixed route trips, and a GoBus route reaches Columbus and Wooster. Dawes Arboretum lies south of town, and C-TEC runs career programs for teens and adults.

Homes in older neighborhoods may fall in a historic area, such as the Hudson Avenue Historic District. An owner of an older house gains by collecting permits, receipts for roof or furnace work and renovation notes, because buyers ask for them before they offer.

Which Newark offices and permits matter before you list?

Property maintenance enforcement belongs to the Department of Public Safety. Code 07-03 took effect January 17, 2007 and was amended June 17, 2008. It follows the International Property Maintenance Code, modified for Newark. Complaints go to the division by email or phone, and in-person visits are by appointment.

The Division of Zoning, at 40 W. Main Street, issues permits under a fee schedule dated November 1, 2023. A few entries bear on a sale or a cleanout:

  • Residential demolition permit: $75
  • Accessory structure permit: $30
  • Temporary storage unit, pod or bin: $30
  • Residential addition: $50
  • Board of Zoning Appeals variance for a one or two family dwelling: $75
  • Lot split, combination or re-plat: $50

Fees can change, so check them with the division.

How is a Newark house sale recorded in Licking County?

At 20 South Second Street in Newark, the Licking County Auditor serves the public weekdays between 8:30 and 4:30. Since May 1, 2026, same-day processing of property transfers stops at 4 p.m.; the covered transfers are conveyances, exempts, splits and merges. Papers delivered later wait for the next business day.

The Recorder's fee page adds a $5.00 preservation surcharge on each standard document as of January 1, 2025. Under R.C. 319.202 the buyer files a value statement, and the seller pays the conveyance fee along with any county transfer tax. A county may set that tax up to thirty cents per hundred dollars (R.C. 322.02), so request the Licking County rate that applies on your closing date.

What can a Newark buyer demand in disclosures?

R.C. 5302.30 has the seller of a one to four unit home fill out the state commerce department's disclosure form and pass it to the buyer. Should it arrive after an offer is made, the buyer holds a three business day right to cancel in writing, which expires at the earlier of 30 days post-acceptance or closing.

A signed form given before the offer removes that rescission option. The statute carves out exemptions, such as sales by an estate fiduciary, and allows a buyer to waive the cancellation right, so read contract wording closely.

Who handles tax values and relief programs in Licking County?

Licking County's auditor values property for tax purposes and transfers deeds, and also serves as secretary to the Board of Revision and the Budget Commission. The same office runs the tax reduction programs. An owner currently receiving a reduction should tell the buyer and title company, since the next owner has to qualify separately.

Contact the auditor's Newark office about your parcel before closing, and ask the treasurer whether a balance remains on the current bill.

When does a direct cash sale suit a Newark house?

A direct sale may suit an owner stuck with a probate house, a landlord leaving a worn rental, or a seller whose home needs work city inspectors would flag. It may also help when a short closing timeline runs up against the 4 p.m. transfer cutoff.

Ask any buyer how closing costs are divided, what the title company charges and whether the price moves after an inspection. Get the terms in a written contract before you move out.

Where is a Newark deed recorded?

The auditor transfers it at 20 South Second Street and the Recorder then records it. Same-day property transfers have a 4 p.m. cutoff, in place since May 1, 2026.

What is the median home value in Newark?

QuickFacts lists $192,300 as the midpoint for owned homes. Any one house may fall far off that number, depending on its condition.

Does tearing down a shed in Newark need a permit?

The city's fee schedule shows $25 for demolishing an accessory structure. Phone the Division of Zoning to confirm the fee and whether your project requires one.

How can I report a code problem in Newark?

Email or call the Division of Property Maintenance Enforcement. It enforces Code 07-03, which is built on the International Property Maintenance Code.

What does Ohio require me to tell a Newark buyer?

Most owners selling one to four unit homes complete the state property disclosure form (R.C. 5302.30) and give each prospective buyer a signed copy. If the form comes late, the buyer has three business days after getting it to cancel.

What does a Cuyahoga Falls house sale involve from start to finish?

Most owners hire a listing agent, though some handle the sale alone or deal with a buyer who closes on the house in its present condition. Each route ends at the same desks in Summit County. Buyer and seller sign the city's stormwater disclosure, someone prepares a deed, and the county Fiscal Office transfers and records it. The routes differ in how long the wait runs, who pays for repairs, and how much uncertainty the seller absorbs.

Cuyahoga Falls lies directly north of Akron and is the second-largest city in Summit County. The Census Bureau gives it 25.80 square miles of land, 51,114 residents in the 2020 count and an estimate of 50,975 for July 2025. Measured against the 2020 estimates base, that is a slip of 0.2 percent, which describes a settled city.

How does the city's past affect the houses on the market?

A river power town became a residential suburb, and that history explains both the street pattern and the school boundaries. Settlers dammed the Cuyahoga River in 1812 to run mills, and the community was first called Manchester before the Post Office pushed a rename. By the middle of the twentieth century the mills had faded and the city was mostly homes.

Census tallies show the speed of the change: 20,546 residents in 1940, then 47,922 by 1960. A house from those decades invites buyer questions about sewer laterals, gutters and downspouts, the very items the city's stormwater inspection examines.

In 1986 the city merged with Northampton Township, the first merger of a city and a township in Ohio. The former township land lies in the northwest and kept its own school district, so describe a northwest property by the right district name.

What do federal housing statistics show for Cuyahoga Falls?

Owners hold a majority here. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $183,300, and 64.4 percent of the city's 23,212 households own their homes (Census Bureau QuickFacts, 2020 through 2024).

  • Renters pay a median gross rent of $1,038 a month.
  • Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,349; those without one report $578.
  • Median household income is $72,705, and the average commute takes 21.6 minutes.
  • The 2020 Census counted 24,827 housing units, 5.7 percent of them vacant.

The homeowner vacancy rate was only 1.1 percent in 2020, so an owner-occupied house that needs work often sits beside tidier listings aimed at the same buyers.

Four school districts reach into Cuyahoga Falls

The Cuyahoga Falls City School District covers nearly all of the original city area, with its high school near downtown, and it also takes in the village of Silver Lake.

The former Northampton Township area is served by Woodridge Local School District, whose high school is in Cuyahoga Falls even though its mailing address says Peninsula. A small slice of the northeast is zoned to Hudson City School District, and a sliver of the far northwest is in Revere Local School District. Verify the district for your parcel before a listing names one.

What does the city's stormwater inspection require at sale?

The city offers a free stormwater inspection, and every house sale there needs the buyer and the seller to sign off on the related disclosure. The inspection looks for clean water getting into the sanitary sewer from private property, such as downspouts or footer drains tied to the wrong pipe. Anything that violates city code must be repaired within 180 days after the inspection.

Chapter 1306 of the city's codified ordinances sets the mechanics:

  • The owner, or a buyer under contract, may ask the city to inspect sewer laterals, sewer connections, gutters, downspouts and footer drains.
  • The city does the work at its own cost and may use a sewer camera, smoke or dye testing.
  • A Certificate of Inspection reaches the owner within ten days, and the requesting buyer too when a buyer asked.
  • Once an owner holds a certificate, the purchaser must receive a copy before any transfer.
  • After repairs, the owner can request a Certificate of Completion.

The same chapter bars anyone from selling sewer-served property without telling the buyer the inspection exists, on a form from the City Engineer. Breaking the chapter is a fourth-degree misdemeanor. Request forms sit in the housing and development section of the city's permits page.

What if my house has open code problems?

The city's housing division enforces property maintenance and zoning rules through inspections and complaint investigations. Complaints can be made anonymously, and each one is tracked. The development department takes calls at (330) 971-8135.

The city names these as the most frequent violations:

  • overgrown weeds, trees or shrubbery in the yard;
  • trash and refuse left outside;
  • abandoned or inoperable vehicles, boats and trailers;
  • garages, sheds, fences or houses in poor structural repair;
  • pet waste left on the ground.

Mowing a yard or hauling off a derelict trailer costs far less than negotiating around it after a buyer's walk-through. An inherited house that has stood empty is a common place for these items to pile up.

What does the Ohio disclosure statute add?

Section 5302.30 of the Ohio Revised Code applies to residential property with one to four units. The owner fills out the state form and delivers a signed copy to the buyer promptly. If the form first arrives after a contract exists, the buyer gets three business days from receipt to cancel in writing, and the right ends at thirty days after acceptance or at closing, whichever comes first.

Some transfers fall outside the rule, including court-ordered sales and sales by an estate's fiduciary. An heir who took the house by inheritance and never lived in it during the prior year is also exempt, which describes many Summit County estate sales.

What are the Summit County transfer and recording charges?

The Fiscal Office posts a transfer charge and a separate recording charge on its fee page and recording FAQ.

Summit County Fiscal Office charges for a sale (source: Fiscal Office fee page and recording FAQ)
ItemRate as posted
Conveyance fee$4.00 per $1000, with the sale price rounded up to the next $100
Lot fee50 cents for each lot named in the legal description
Recording a deed$34 covers two pages; each added page costs $8
Copy of a recorded deed$4, and $1 more for a certified copy
Recording turnaround3 to 5 working days

The recording division does no title or property searches, which leaves that work to your title company. A name change on a recorded deed needs a new deed, and Ohio law allows only the requester or an attorney to draft it. The office has moved temporarily during construction at its building, so look up the service location on its website before visiting.

When would a cash buyer make sense for a Cuyahoga Falls owner?

An as-is purchase makes sense when a firm closing date counts for more than a top price. Typical cases are a house with unfinished stormwater items, long-deferred upkeep, tenants in place, or a title that still needs sorting after an estate. The buyer takes on those problems, and the seller can often pick a closing day that fits a move.

Set any figure beside the net from a repaired, listed house, the cost of waiting, and the 180-day clock that starts after a stormwater inspection finds violations. Get price, closing day and closing-cost split in writing from each buyer so the offers line up.

More questions about Cuyahoga Falls, OH

Is a stormwater inspection mandatory for a Cuyahoga Falls sale?

The signed disclosure is mandatory, while the inspection itself is free and happens on request. Chapter 1306 lets an owner or a buyer under contract ask for it, and an owner holding a Certificate of Inspection must pass a copy to the buyer.

What is the deadline for fixing stormwater violations?

The city's stormwater page sets 180 days after the inspection. Following repairs, an owner may ask for a Certificate of Completion confirming the listed items were corrected.

What is the recording turnaround in Summit County?

Three to five working days, according to the Fiscal Office. Its recording division lists 330-643-2712, and electronic recording runs through several approved vendors.

How do I find my school district in Cuyahoga Falls?

Cuyahoga Falls City Schools cover the original city, Woodridge Local covers the former Northampton Township, and small corners belong to Hudson City and Revere Local. Match your parcel against county records first.

Can a buyer walk away after reading the state form?

Only when the form arrives late. A buyer who gets it after a contract exists may cancel in writing within three business days, with the right ending by thirty days after acceptance or at closing, whichever is earlier.

How does selling a house in Dublin, Ohio work?

A Dublin seller can list through an agent, sell without one, or take a cash purchase, and the first step is learning which county holds your parcel. Dublin is a Columbus suburb whose boundaries fall within Franklin, Delaware, Union and Madison counties, so deed transfer, valuation and recording depend on the county of record. The Census Bureau counted 49,328 residents in 2020 and estimates 49,094 for July 2025, with 24.44 square miles of land.

The Scioto River runs through the city and cuts gorges into limestone bedrock, which leaves ravines and a few steep cliffs on otherwise flat ground. The city sits on the Glaciated Allegheny Plateau, with elevations from 780 feet where the river leaves the city to about 1,000 feet at Glacier Ridge Metro Park.

How did Dublin grow so quickly?

Dublin went from 681 residents in 1970 to 3,855 in 1980 and 16,366 in 1990, a shift tied to the construction of Interstate 270 and the arrival of corporate headquarters. It was declared a city in August 1987 after passing 5,000 residents. By 2000 the count was 31,392, and by 2020 it reached 49,328.

The name comes from John Shields, an Irishman who partnered with John Sells to survey lots for the village around 1810 and named it after Dublin, Ireland. The Dublin Irish Festival, billed as the largest three-day Irish festival in the world, is held here, and the Memorial Tournament has been played at Muirfield Village Golf Club since 1976.

Since 2020 the city has been redeveloping the Bridge Street District, a 1,100-acre project along the Scioto River with apartments, condominiums, retail and offices. The project includes about 400 apartments and condominiums.

What do the Census figures say about Dublin housing?

Dublin's values and owner rate are both high. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts for 2020 through 2024 show the following.

  • Median value of owner-occupied housing: $563,500.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 77.1 percent, across 17,995 households averaging 2.72 people.
  • Median gross rent: $1,686; median owner cost with a mortgage: $3,055, and $1,349 without one.
  • Median household income: $160,296; bachelor's degree or higher among adults 25 and older: 73.4 percent.
  • Residents living in the same house a year earlier: 92.7 percent; foreign-born residents: 20.5 percent.

A 92.7 percent same-house rate means few households moved into or within the city in the prior year.

Which employers and roads link Dublin to Columbus?

The city is home to the headquarters of Cardinal Health, Wendy's, OCLC, IGS Energy and Stanley Steemer. Wikipedia, citing the city's 2020 financial report, lists the largest local employers as Cardinal Health (4,800), OhioHealth (2,000), Dublin City School District (1,951), CareWorks (1,622), OCLC (750) and Wendy's (725). OhioHealth's Dublin Methodist Hospital is among its operations here.

Interstate 270, called the Outerbelt, and State Route 161 are the main expressways. U.S. Route 33 runs together with Route 161 between the roundabout in the center of Dublin and an interchange near an Ohio University satellite campus. State Routes 257 and 745 run along each side of the Scioto River. The Dublin Link, a pedestrian and cycling bridge, opened in March 2020. COTA runs route 33 to downtown Dublin and the Bridge Street District and an express route 73 at rush hour.

Which school districts serve Dublin houses?

The Dublin City School District serves the city, and the Hilliard City School District serves a portion of it. Dublin City has three high schools (Coffman, Scioto and Jerome), five middle schools (Sells, Davis, Grizzell, Karrer and Eversole) and fifteen elementary schools. Enrollment for the 2020 to 2021 school year was 16,254.

Hilliard runs Washington Elementary School inside Dublin's limits. A listing that names a school should check the attendance area for that parcel, because the attendance boundary rather than the city name determines the school.

What permits does Dublin require for house work before a sale?

Dublin processes residential permit applications online through its Accela Citizen Access portal and an electronic plan review system. The city treats residential projects as those on property with one, two or three family dwelling units. Its list of projects that need permits includes the following.

  • New homes and additions.
  • Interior remodeling, including basement remodels.
  • Decks and porches.
  • Swimming pools and hot tubs.

Permits must be paid for and issued before work starts, and electrical, HVAC and plumbing contractors must be registered where registration is required. The state of Ohio adds a 1 percent surcharge to residential fees other than plumbing and sewer or water fees. If a remodel in your house was done without a permit, ask the city's Building Standards office what it takes to close it out before a buyer's inspection.

What are Dublin's rules on code enforcement and deed restrictions?

Dublin enforces zoning, health, parking, nuisance and sign codes, and it says most violation notices allow ten days to comply, with more time possible in unusual circumstances. A complaint is investigated first, and no action follows if no violation is found. Code Enforcement can be reached at 614.410.4600.

The city separates zoning from private deed restrictions and says it does not generally have standing to enforce a deed restriction. Many Dublin subdivisions have restrictions enforced by an association, so a seller with an association should gather the governing documents and any unpaid dues before listing, since buyers will ask.

Can I rent out a Dublin house short term before selling?

Only on tight terms, and only with a city registration. Dublin's short-term rental ordinance, passed on October 12, 2020, took effect for operators as of November 11, 2020. The city lists its main features below.

Dublin short-term rental rules as listed by the city (source: Code Compliance and Enforcement page)
RuleWhat the city lists
RegistrationAnnual registration required before listing
Annual fee$225, valid through December 31 of the approval year
Rental limitTwo weeks per calendar year, in up to two increments of seven days
First-offense fine$250 for operating without registering
Primary residence proofTwo of five listed documents, such as a driver's license or utility bill

The city also requires insurance verification, a notarized affidavit of compliance and a form submitted before each rental period. The registration number must be posted with any listing.

What county costs apply to a Dublin deed, and what does Ohio require?

For the Delaware County portion of Dublin, the Recorder's fee page lists $39 for the first two pages of a deed, including a $5 preservation surcharge, and $8 for each additional page. The Auditor's forms page carries the Real Property Conveyance Fee Statement, form DTE 100, and the Auditor's 2026 triennial valuation page lists a complaint window running from January 1, 2027, through March 31, 2027, for the Delaware County values. Parcels in Franklin or Union County follow those counties' offices, so ask the county auditor and recorder for the current figures.

Ohio's property disclosure law, R.C. 5302.30, makes the owner of a home with one to four units complete the state form for the buyer. When the buyer gets it late, after contracting, cancellation in writing is open for three business days from receipt and closes by the earlier of thirty days from acceptance or the closing date.

More questions about Dublin, OH

Which county do I deal with when I sell a house in Dublin?

It depends on the parcel. Dublin falls within Franklin, Delaware, Union and Madison counties, so check your tax bill or the county auditor's property search to see which office records your deed.

Can I list my Dublin house on Airbnb to cover the mortgage while it sells?

Only with a city registration and within tight limits. The city allows two weeks per calendar year, charges $225 for annual registration, and lists a $250 fine for operating without registering.

How long do I have to fix a Dublin code violation?

Most notices give ten days, and the city says code enforcement staff can discuss and extend that time when circumstances are unusual. You can call Code Enforcement at 614.410.4600.

Does the city enforce my neighborhood's deed restrictions?

Generally not. The city says it does not have standing to pursue enforcement of deed restrictions, so those fall to an association or neighbors. City zoning rules are separate.

What is Dublin's median home value?

The Census Bureau lists a median value of $563,500 for owner-occupied homes in Dublin for 2020 through 2024, with an owner-occupied rate of 77.1 percent.

Sell Your Lakewood House for Cash

Lakewood at a glance

Selling in Lakewood?

Get My Cash Offer →

What changes when a Lakewood owner sells a rental or a worn house?

Lakewood adds a city step for landlords: an owner who sells a non-owner-occupied rental needs a certificate of code compliance, which depends on a point of sale inspection. The certificate rule applies to non-owner occupied rentals. For an owner living in the house, the choice runs among an agent, a by owner sale and a cash buyer.

  • Agent listing: reaches the most buyers for a tidy, updated house, with weeks set aside for inspections and financing.
  • Sale by owner: you set the price, run tours and complete the disclosure paperwork.
  • Cash buyer: takes the house in whatever shape it is in, which suits a double with deferred repairs, a rental with a pending inspection, or a house left by an estate.

Because only 44.4 percent of Lakewood homes are owner occupied, buyers and sellers here see rentals, doubles and small apartment buildings often. Knowing the city's rental rules early keeps a closing date from sliding.

Why does Lakewood have so many older houses?

Lakewood grew as one of Cleveland's streetcar suburbs. The area was surveyed as Rockport Township in 1806 and incorporated as a village in 1889, named for its place on Lake Erie. Streetcars reached it on Detroit Avenue in 1893, Clifton Boulevard in 1903 and Madison Avenue in 1916, and the population jumped from 3,355 in 1900 to 70,509 by 1930. That is why the nickname is City of Homes.

Neighborhoods carry distinct building stock. Birdtown, an eight street district on the southeast side with bird names, was built in the 1890s for National Carbon Company workers and joined the National Register in 2006. Clifton Park in the northwest corner holds Victorian mansions near the lake, and Victorian Village on the east end housed company executives. Rockport Square added roughly 200 condos and lofts from 2004 along Detroit Avenue, and the Gold Coast high rises sit on the lakefront.

Lakewood is dense, with 9,190 people per square mile on only 5.54 square miles of land. That density shows up in the small lots and close neighbors a buyer will see on every block.

How does Lakewood's population profile differ from its neighbors?

The Census Bureau puts Lakewood at 49,027 people on July 1, 2025, a 3.7 percent decline from the 2020 base of 50,930. The table shows other traits that set Lakewood apart.

Lakewood and Kent compared in Census QuickFacts, with the 2020 land area and 2020 to 2024 survey figures

People per household1.852.14
Land area, square miles (2020)5.549.22
Adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree55.3%47.1%

Of Kent, Kettering, Lancaster and Lakewood, Lakewood has the top median home value and the smallest households, at 1.85 people. Small households and a high renter share reflect a city of apartments, doubles and compact single family homes.

How do Lakewood schools, roads and the lakefront shape a sale?

Public schools belong to the Lakewood City School District: Lakewood High School, Garfield and Harding middle schools and seven elementary schools. The district rebuilt or renovated its buildings in a program finished in 2017, the first major school construction program since 1920. Private options include Lakewood Catholic Academy and St. Edward High School.

  • Highways: Interstate 90 runs along the south side with ramps at West 117th Street, Bunts Road, Warren Road and McKinley Road.
  • Transit: Greater Cleveland RTA buses cover Clifton Boulevard, Detroit Avenue, Madison Avenue, Warren Road and West 117th Street, and Red Line rapid stations sit just across the Cleveland border.
  • Lakefront and parks: Lakewood Park is one of the largest lakefront parks in Ohio, and the Rocky River Reservation of the Cleveland Metroparks forms part of the western edge.

A Cleveland Clinic family health center opened in 2018 across the street from the former Lakewood Hospital site. Downtown Cleveland is about 6 miles to the east.

What does the city require before a Lakewood rental changes hands?

Lakewood requires a housing license for any dwelling unit rented to another person, and the Housing and Building Department collects the fees. The city's page lists $75.00 per unit for non-owner occupied one or two family structures, $60.00 per unit for three family dwellings, $45.00 per unit for other non-owner occupied dwellings, and $200.00 per building for a vacant property license. Owners who miss the November 1 deadline pay a $25.00 late fee per unit.

Since September 1, 2019, a certificate of code compliance is required before the sale of any non-owner occupied residential rental property. The point of sale inspection covers the interior, exterior and yard before the certificate issues, and the rules sit in Lakewood Codified Ordinances sections 1173.01 and 1306.53. To schedule one, call the Division of Housing and Building at (216) 529-6270 or write to building.permits@lakewoodoh.gov.

Start this process before you sign a purchase contract. An inspector's list of repairs is far easier to handle when you know about it at the start of a sale than at the closing table.

How are deeds and rental registrations handled in Cuyahoga County?

Lakewood is in Cuyahoga County, where the Fiscal Officer's Real Estate Services office handles transfers and recording at 2079 E. Ninth Street, fourth floor, Cleveland. The office page lists weekday hours and a recording cutoff of 4:00 p.m., so plan to arrive early. Each transfer needs a DTE 100 statement of value or a DTE 100 EX exemption statement. The standard recording charge, raised on October 24, 2024 under Senate Bill 94, is $39 for the opening pair of pages plus $8 per added page.

A separate county duty falls on rental owners. Ohio Revised Code 5323.02 requires a one time filing with the Fiscal Officer, with no fee, and any change must be reported within 60 days. The county says a $50 penalty can follow each tax bill when the filing is missing, and that this filing is needed even if the city has the rental on record. A buyer of your rental will need to file, and under Revised Code 319.202 the auditor's endorsement on the conveyance flags this.

Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 requires the property disclosure form on one to four unit residential sales, with exceptions for fiduciary transfers and sales to a buyer who occupied the property for twelve months. For the conveyance fee rate that applies in Cuyahoga County, ask the Fiscal Officer before closing.

More questions about Lakewood, OH

Does a Lakewood rental need an inspection before it can be sold?

Yes. Lakewood's code requires a certificate of code compliance before the sale of a non-owner occupied residential rental, and a point of sale inspection comes first. Call (216) 529-6270 to schedule it.

What does a Lakewood housing license cost?

The city lists $75.00 per unit for non-owner occupied one or two family structures, $60.00 per unit for three family dwellings, and $45.00 per unit for other non-owner occupied dwellings. Late applications after November 1 add $25.00 per unit.

Where do deeds for Lakewood houses get filed?

They go to the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Officer's Transfer and Recording office in Cleveland. A DTE 100 or DTE 100 EX form has to accompany the deed.

Is the disclosure form still required when a Lakewood house sells as is?

Usually yes. Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 covers sales of homes with up to four dwelling units, and calling the sale as is does not replace the form. Estate fiduciaries and several other transfers are exempt.

Does the buyer of my Lakewood rental have to register it with the county?

Yes, a new owner of residential rental property files with the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Officer under Revised Code 5323.02, even when the rental is already registered with the city. There is no filing fee, but a $50 penalty can follow each tax bill if the filing is missing.
