From 1887 to 1905 the Lima field produced about 300 million barrels, a trunk pipeline reached Chicago within three years, and the refinery established in 1886 is still operating after more than 125 years under a string of owners. Locomotives, trucks and buses came next, and the Superior Coach Company grew into the world's largest maker of school buses and funeral coaches.

The 1970s through the 1990s were harder. Clark Equipment and Superior Coach shut in 1981, Airfoil Textron followed in 1985, and the city lost more than 8,000 jobs by the mid 1990s while its population fell from about 52,000 to about 45,000. Houses built for that workforce are what many sellers now hold.

Which employers keep Lima running?

Hospitals, a tank factory, a refinery and three colleges hold up the local economy. Mercy Health St. Rita's Medical Center and Lima Memorial Health System each run a level 2 trauma center and together draw patients from a ten-county region.

The Joint Systems Manufacturing Center, better known as the Lima Army Tank Plant, opened in 1941 and is the only maker of the M1 Abrams. Health care and social assistance brought in about $986.7 million in 2022 according to the Census Bureau, well ahead of the city's $522.1 million in retail sales. Ohio State University at Lima, James A. Rhodes State College and the University of Northwestern Ohio supply student renters.

Short commutes help a Lima listing. With an average of 17.1 minutes to work, a house near a hospital campus or the interstate ramps can be pitched as convenient.

Which roads and schools should appear in a Lima listing?

Ohio routes 309, 65, 81 and 117 cross in Lima, Interstate 75 runs along its eastern side, and U.S. Route 30 lies a few miles to the north. The Lima Allen County Airport is about 5.8 miles southeast of downtown.

For high school, public students look to Lima Senior High School, and Apollo Career Center covers technical programs. Lima Central Catholic High School, Lima Christian Academy and Temple Christian School serve families who choose private schooling. Because attendance zones can change, quote the school district's own assignment tool instead of repeating what a neighbor says.

  • Highlight the quick run to Interstate 75 for commuters.
  • Name the nearest hospital campus when it is within a few minutes.
  • Check the street's school assignment with the district before printing it.

What does Ohio require a Lima seller to sign and file?

Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 obliges owners of one-to-four unit homes to hand each prospective buyer a completed disclosure form. A buyer who receives it only after contracting has three business days to cancel in writing.

Court-ordered transfers, foreclosure sales and estate transfers by a fiduciary sit outside the rule, as does a sale by someone who inherited the house and has not lived there in the last year. If your Lima house came through probate, have the closing office confirm which side of that line you are on.

The conveyance fee belongs to the seller. Section 319.202 puts the grantor on the hook, and section 319.54 prints the base fee as one dollar or ten cents per hundred dollars, whichever is greater. Counties may add their own tax under section 322.02 at up to thirty cents per hundred dollars, so ask the Allen County Auditor which rate applies to your deed.

Must Lima landlords register every rental unit?

Yes. A Lima ordinance passed on January 2, 2024 requires each owner of a rental housing unit to hold a Rental Housing Unit Registration Certificate, and that duty applies even when the unit sits empty.

The city phased the deadlines by portfolio size: June 30, 2024 for ten or more units, December 31, 2024 for five to nine, and June 30, 2025 for one to four. Every one of those dates is behind us. Registration and updates carry no fee, and owners file through online forms after opening a CivicPlus account, as described in the city's registration notice.

Sales trigger a follow-up. A buyer who takes over a registered unit has 30 days after closing to update the record, so a landlord selling to an investor should pass along the certificate details.

  • Single-property and multi-property online forms both exist.
  • An unrented unit still needs a certificate.
  • Separate from the city rule, owners also report contact details to the county auditor.

What happens at the Allen County Auditor and Recorder?

Your deed visits two county offices in order. The auditor stamps it for transfer, and then the recorder places it in the permanent land records. The recorder's page says mailed conveyances are taken only when the auditor's conveyance stamp is already affixed.

The recorder's duties include deeds, mortgages, plats, powers of attorney and tax delinquency liens, each indexed so a title searcher can trace ownership. A document showing a Social Security number is turned away unless an affidavit comes with it. Recording fees follow the Revised Code and are printed in a schedule the office publishes, so request the current sheet before closing.

Drafting the deed and clearing old mortgages belongs to a title company or attorney. County staff explain their own steps but cannot write your documents.

What do cold Lima winters mean for a sale?

They put heating systems, roofs and basements under the microscope. Lima's January daily mean is about 26 degrees Fahrenheit against about 73 in July, and snowfall peaks in January.

Buyers' inspectors in a four-season climate like this often flag shingles, gutters, foundation walls and furnaces first. Documenting recent work on those items, or pricing the house to reflect their age, prevents surprises. A vacant house that sits through a freeze needs steady heat or drained pipes.

More questions about Lima, OH

Can I sell my Lima house without making repairs?

Yes. Ohio sets no repair requirement for a sale, though the disclosure form must still be delivered unless your transfer is exempt. Investors who buy for cash typically price the repairs into their offer.

Who covers the transfer charges on a Lima sale?

The seller pays them. The grantor owes the state conveyance fee and any county transfer tax under section 319.202(D). Your contract may allocate other closing costs differently.

What if I rent the house I want to sell?

Confirm the city certificate is current before you list. Lima requires a rental registration for each unit, and the incoming owner must update it within 30 days of closing. County auditor contact filings are a separate duty.

Where do Lima deeds get recorded?

With the Allen County Recorder, after the Allen County Auditor stamps the document. Both are county offices located in the city, and neither is part of city hall.

What slows down a Lima closing the most?

Title problems and lender steps cause most delays. Open liens, an unsettled estate or a missing signature can hold up the auditor stamp and recording, while a cash buyer removes the appraisal and underwriting stages.

Which route gets a Stow house sold with the least friction?

Pick the route that fits the problem. A tidy Stow house can ride the open market, but one with a failing roof, a stubborn tenant or an unsettled estate may suit a buyer who accepts it unrepaired.

All three finish with a deed filed through the county, so a title company or attorney should be on board from the start.

What is Stow like as a place to sell?

Stow is an Akron suburb on the Summit and Portage county line. Joshua Stow, a Connecticut native who never lived here, bought the 25-square-mile township in the Western Reserve survey. William Walker arrived as the first settler in 1802, and the township joined the new Summit County in 1840. Cuyahoga Falls, Munroe Falls and Silver Lake were later carved from its land, and what remained became a village in 1957.

Kent sits to the east, Tallmadge and Munroe Falls to the south, Hudson to the north and Cuyahoga Falls to the west, and shoppers tend to compare every one of them. The city covers 17.09 square miles of land and 0.23 of water.

Summers run warm and muggy and winters run cold. Stow is outside the main Lake Erie snowbelt but inside the secondary snowbelt, so heavier lake-effect snow shows up when the wind runs a certain way. An inspector will likely dwell on the roof, gutters, furnace and basement.

Three state routes serve the city: Ohio 8, Ohio 59 along Kent Road and Ohio 91 along Darrow Road. METRO RTA and PARTA buses stop in Stow, and Kent State University Airport is also located here.

What do Stow's Census figures say about the housing market?

Who is buying and living in Stow houses?

Stow's median age at the 2020 census was 41.6. Seniors made up 19.7 percent of the population, children under 18 made up 20.0 percent, and about three in ten of the 14,608 households were someone living alone.

QuickFacts reports a bachelor's degree or more for 48.0 percent of adults, plus a mean commute of 23.5 minutes and a poverty rate of 5.2 percent. Highway access is therefore a fair talking point in a listing, since Ohio 8 runs through town.

Which schools and parks do Stow buyers ask about?

The Stow-Munroe Falls City School District covers Stow and most of Munroe Falls. Its elementary buildings are Echo Hills, Fishcreek, Highland, Indian Trail, Riverview and Woodland, followed by Lakeview Intermediate, Kimpton Middle and Stow-Munroe Falls High School. Holy Family School is the Catholic choice for first through eighth grade.

Outdoor space gives listings extra weight:

  • Adell Durbin Park, Meadowbrook Lake Park, Silver Springs Park and Oregon Trail Park.
  • Fox Den Golf Course, which the city owns, and Roses Run Country Club beside the Cuyahoga River.
  • The paved Bike and Hike trail from Summit County MetroParks, 33.5 miles long, running through Stow toward Brandywine Falls.

Ground was broken on April 12, 2026 for an amphitheater called The AMP, with a finish date planned for the end of that year.

Do Stow permits and inspections affect a sale?

Sometimes, through unfinished work. If a buyer's inspector notices a newer deck, furnace, roof or finished basement, expect a request to see the permit. Pull your records before listing and close out whatever is still open.

The Stow Building Department runs permits and construction inspections, and its online portal accepts forms, inspection requests and contractor registrations at any hour. A call in before 9 am gets same-day inspection, and electric and plumbing visits happen on Monday, Wednesday and Thursday mornings. The department's line is 330-689-2729. Engineering, which handles drawings and the public right-of-way side of projects, is reached at 330-689-2719.

Stow's building office does not issue sanitary sewer permits. Those come from the Summit County Department of Sanitary Services, 1180 S Main Street in Akron, so call them about any sewer lateral question before closing. The Ohio Board of Building Standards writes the state codes that the city enforces.

What happens at the Summit County Fiscal Office when a Stow deed transfers?

The Fiscal Office's Property Transfer Department checks the legal description and approves the conveyance. Every deed travels with a DTE 100 statement of value, or a DTE 100 (EX) when an exemption applies. Paperwork received by 3:30 PM can be approved that same day.

The Fiscal Office fee page prints three lines that matter at closing:

  • Conveyance Fee: $4.00 per $1000 rounded up to the next $100 of the sale price.
  • Lot Fee: 50 cents per lot contained in the legal description.
  • Basic recording: $34.00 for two pages, $8.00 for each additional page.

Under Ohio Revised Code 322.02 the county's transfer tax falls on the grantor, who pays the auditor at delivery of the deed. Have the closing agent check your settlement statement against these lines.

Which disclosure form applies to a Stow seller?

Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 requires the state's property disclosure form for houses with up to four units. Hand each prospective buyer a signed, dated copy early, because a buyer who gets it late can rescind in writing. The form asks about water, sewer, structure and hazards such as radon and lead paint.

Fill in each item in good faith. Where you truly lack the facts, the statute allows a good-faith approximation.

When is a cash offer worth considering in Stow?

A direct purchase suits an estate house with deferred repairs, a rental with a tenant, or an owner who has moved away and is carrying two sets of bills. If a roof or sewer line is near the end of its life, an as-is buyer spares you the repair decision.

Compare any figure with the net from a listing after commission and repairs. Ask who covers the transfer charge, how long the title work runs and what happens if the buyer walks away, then get every answer in the contract.

More questions about Stow, OH

Who pays the county transfer charge on a Stow sale?

You do, as the seller. Ohio Revised Code 322.02 puts the county transfer tax on the grantor, and the Summit County auditor side of the Fiscal Office takes payment when the deed comes in.

What inspections does the City of Stow perform?

Permit inspections on construction work, with same-day service for calls before 9 am. Check with the Building Department at 330-689-2729 about your address, and plan on the buyer ordering a private inspection.

Which office records a Stow deed?

A Stow address falls under Summit County, which means the Fiscal Office records the instrument after the transfer step. Ask for the per-page recording charge when you schedule the closing.

Can I sell a Stow house that has a tenant?

Yes. Hand the buyer the lease and the deposit ledger, or set a vacate date in the contract. Landlord-tenant duties continue until the day title changes hands.

What if I inherited a house in Stow?

Start by learning who is legally allowed to sign. The probate court and the Fiscal Office can say which affidavit or certificate moves title out of the decedent's name, and an Ohio probate attorney can sort out the rest before you accept an offer.

What should a Westlake seller line up before listing?

Westlake is a Cuyahoga County suburb about 12 miles west of downtown Cleveland. The city spans 15.93 square miles of land, and the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate of 33,904 people is 1.0% under its 2020 base. City Hall sits at 27700 Hilliard Boulevard, phone 440-871-3300, open 8 am to 4 pm.

For permits and property maintenance, ask City Hall directly. For deeds and value complaints, use the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office and Board of Revision. The sections below explain what each office does and what the market data shows.

How did Dover Township become Westlake?

European settlers first arrived on October 10, 1810, when the area belonged to Dover Township. Bay Village split off in 1901, and a southern piece joined North Olmsted in 1912. The remaining residents formed Dover Village in 1913. The name changed to Westlake in 1940 to avoid confusion with Dover in Tuscarawas County, and Westlake became a city in 1957.

Growth came fast after that, and each census shows the pace:

  • 1950: 4,912 residents, and 1960: 12,906.
  • 1970: 15,689, and 1980: 19,475.
  • 1990: 27,018, and 2000: 31,719.
  • 2010: 32,729, and 2020: 34,228.

The 2025 Census estimates put residents under 18 at 20.2% and children under five at 4.6%. The 2020 census counted 15,508 housing units in the city, 5.7% of them vacant.

What does a Westlake home cost to own, and who lives here?

Census figures averaged over 2020 through 2024 describe an older suburb where most households own.

  • 73.1% of homes are occupied by their owners, and the middle value among them is $368,200.
  • Owners with a mortgage spend $2,071 a month on housing; owners without one spend $926.
  • Renters pay $1,570 a month at the midpoint.
  • 14,424 households share the city, averaging 2.29 people.
  • Half of households earn more than $112,200, and 60.2% of adults over 25 hold at least a four-year degree.
  • 25.1% of residents are 65 or older, and the 2020 census put the median age at 47.4.

With that age profile, many Westlake sales involve owners downsizing or heirs settling an estate. Foreign-born residents account for 12.6% of the city.

Which employers and shopping districts support Westlake home values?

Westlake is a headquarters town. Nordson, American Greetings, Hyland Software, Scott Fetzer, TravelCenters of America and Equity Trust are all based here. In the city's 2021 financial report, University Hospitals Health System leads with 3,202 workers, then Hyland Software with 1,987 and American Greetings with 1,167. Lower on the list sit TA Operating at 835 workers, the Westlake City School District at 707 and the City of Westlake itself at 413, so the local job base spans health care, software, retail and public service.

Crocker Park, a mixed-use center built around a small-town street plan, holds 1,050,000 square feet of retail, 650 residential units and 100,000 square feet of office space. Westlake commuters average 24.4 minutes each way, and downtown Cleveland lies 12 miles east.

How does a deed move through the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office?

A Westlake deed does not go to a city office. It goes to the county Fiscal Office, where the Transfer and Recording division holds the duties of the former auditor, recorder and engineer. The phone number is 216-443-2060.

  • Each transfer must arrive with one of two state forms: the DTE 100 value statement and receipt, or the DTE 100-EX explaining why the conveyance fee is exempt.
  • Staff cannot draft your deed. The county treats that as legal work, so have the document prepared by a title company or attorney.

When can you dispute your Westlake property value?

The Cuyahoga County Board of Revision decides complaints about real property valuation under Chapter 5715 of the Revised Code. Filing for tax year 2025 is over, and the period for tax year 2026 runs January 1 to March 31, 2027. By statute the cutoff is the end of March after the tax year, or the close of first-half collection when that comes later.

The board works from the second floor at 2079 East Ninth Street, phone 216-443-7195, email BORInfo@cuyahogacounty.gov. Its site posts the state forms, a searchable list of closed and pending complaints since 2018 and guidance on evidence. Ohio Revised Code 5715.19 requires a complainant to give the board all information or evidence they hold that affects the property.

Read the evidence guidance on the board's site before you file, since a complainant who withholds evidence can be barred from using it on appeal.

What did the 2020 census show about Westlake households?

The 2020 count found 14,618 households living in 15,508 housing units, with 5.7% of units vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.8% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.5%, so few owner-occupied homes stood empty while apartments sat open more often.

  • Married couples headed 49.4% of households.
  • Single-person households made up 35.3%, and 16.3% were someone 65 or older living alone.
  • Only 22.8% of households had children under 18.

The Westlake City School District serves the city's families with children.

How do your options compare for a quick Westlake sale?

A typical owner-occupied value of $368,200 points to buyers who finance with a mortgage, which ties the timeline to their lender. A direct as-is purchase can close on a date you pick, at a price that reflects the repairs involved.

  • Get each offer on paper with the closing date, the party paying closing costs and any repair exclusions.
  • Ask any cash buyer for proof of funds first.
  • Compare the amount left after paying off a mortgage and unpaid property tax, since the headline price overstates your proceeds.

What should you ask City Hall before listing a Westlake house?

The city's Codified Ordinances are posted on American Legal Publishing, with the version on file current through July 16, 2026. Rather than guess at local rules, put the same short list of questions to City Hall.

  • Is there an open permit, or one that never received a final inspection?
  • If the house is a rental, does the city require a license or registration, and does it pass to a new owner?
  • Are there any open property maintenance or zoning complaints?
  • Which sewer and water accounts need a final reading at closing?
  • Do you have the signed state disclosure form ready? Section 5302.30 of the Revised Code makes sellers of one-to-four unit homes deliver it, with exceptions for estates and some family transfers.

Record each answer with the date and the department. The title company handling the closing is likely to ask the same questions.

By when must a Westlake value complaint be filed?

The end of March following the tax year. For tax year 2026 the Board of Revision lists January 1 through March 31, 2027. Call 216-443-7195 with questions.

What is Crocker Park?

A mixed-use center in Westlake built around a small-town street plan. It holds 1,050,000 square feet of retail, 650 residential units and 100,000 square feet of office space.

How far is Westlake from downtown Cleveland?

About 12 miles west. Census data lists an average commute of 24.4 minutes for Westlake workers, so a buyer who works downtown will still weigh drive time.

Why is the city called Westlake?

Dover Village took the name in 1940 to avoid confusion with Dover in Tuscarawas County. Westlake became a city in 1957.

How much has Westlake's population changed?

What are the ways to sell a house fast in Massillon, Ohio?

Massillon owners can hire a broker, go it alone, or accept a straight cash purchase. After a contract is signed, every route goes through the Stark County Auditor and the county recorder, and through Massillon's code enforcement if the property has open violations.

Condition decides a lot here. A house with deferred work can lose weeks to inspection requests on a conventional sale. A buyer paying cash typically prices the work in and skips the repair negotiation.

  • Agent listing: wider exposure, and a commission plus repair talks.
  • Owner sale: lower cost, but the pricing and paperwork are yours.
  • Cash buyer: a single negotiated number and a closing date you can usually influence.

What do Census numbers show for Massillon housing?

Massillon had an estimated 32,168 residents on July 1, 2025, 0.5 percent above the April 2020 base. The housing figures for 2020-2024 are summarized in the table.

Residents 65 and older make up 20.2 percent of the city, and the 2020 census found 14,777 housing units, 7.8 percent of them vacant.

How did Massillon's history shape its streets and houses?

Massillon grew along the Tuscarawas River and the Ohio and Erie Canal. Thomas Rotch founded the settlement of Kendal in 1812, and James Duncan recorded the plat for Massillon on December 6, 1826, naming it for a French bishop at his wife's request.

Industry followed. Russell and Company built threshing machines and steam traction engines, and the Massillon Rolling Mill Company rolled its first sheet of steel in 1909. By 1959, Republic Steel's Massillon operations employed nearly half of the city's workforce.

Main Street became Lincoln Way when the Lincoln Highway came through, and a limited-access U.S. 30 bypass opened in 1971, which moved through traffic to the city's southern edge. Massillon lies about 8 miles west of Canton, 20 miles south of Akron and 50 miles south of Cleveland.

Which Massillon neighborhoods and townships matter for a sale?

Massillon spreads over the western half of Perry Township and reaches into Jackson, Tuscarawas and Bethlehem townships, with the village of Navarre on its southern border. The township and school district behind a parcel set its levies, so read the parcel record before choosing a price.

Residential neighborhoods listed for Massillon include:

  • Moffitt Heights, Perry Heights, Sippo Heights, Kendall Heights and Amherst Heights.
  • Oak Ridge, Walnut Hills, Colonial Hills, Chestnut Hills and Elms Acres.
  • Lawndale, Clearview, Greenwood Acres, West Park and University Village.

Massillon Washington High School is home to the Tigers football program, and the R. G. Drage Career Technical Center serves students across western Stark County. Paul Brown Tiger Stadium seats 16,884 and was completed in 1939.

What local landmarks and institutions anchor Massillon?

The Massillon Museum opened in 1933 and now occupies the historic Gensemer Brothers Dry Goods building downtown. Its collection holds about 100,000 objects, including the Immel Circus, a miniature of 2,620 pieces.

Spring Hill, the home of Thomas and Charity Rotch, opened to the public in 1973 and now interprets their Underground Railroad work. The Lions Lincoln Theatre, a 1915 movie house saved from demolition in 1982, still screens films and hosts live theatre.

The Massillon Municipal Court serves western Stark County, and the Massillon State Hospital, opened in 1898 on 240 acres, is now called Heartland Behavioral Healthcare.

What does Massillon's economy look like for homeowners?

Manufacturing and food processing still employ many residents. Shearer's Foods, Sugardale, Fresh Mark, Aqua Ohio, Midwestern Industries and NFM Welding are among the companies named as based or prominent in the city, and the central business district runs along Lincoln Way.

Outdoor options are also close. The city's parks department runs a recreation center, a senior center and 35 parks and open spaces, and the Ohio and Erie Canal Towpath Trail and the Sippo Valley Bike and Hike Trail both pass through.

Commutes are short: QuickFacts gives 21.5 minutes as the mean trip to work for Massillon residents.

What does Massillon require of rental, vacant and foreclosed properties?

Massillon's Code Enforcement Department runs the city's registration program for non-owner-occupied (rental), vacant and foreclosed properties. It also enforces rules on rubbish, junk vehicles, vegetation, dangerous buildings and building permit problems, and it keeps an online case search where you can look up a violation.

Before you sell, look up your address there. An open case can slow a sale, and a decision by the department can be appealed to the Board of Building Appeals.

Rentals carry one more step under Ohio Revised Code 5323.02, a contact filing with the county auditor. Stark County sets the filing deadline at 60 days after a conveyance form reaches the auditor, with a penalty of up to $150 against the parcel if it is missed.

What does the Stark County Auditor check on a Massillon deed?

Every parcel presented for transfer in Stark County first has its legal description checked by the auditor's Tax Map Department against the county's Standards Governing Conveyances. The deed itself must also meet the department's Deed Requirement Guidelines.

The same department reviews splits, combinations, easement plats, annexations and condominium declarations, and it approves legal descriptions for sheriff sales. Its number is 330-451-7341, and it states that it cannot give legal advice or recommend private surveyors, title offices or attorneys.

Ask the Stark County Auditor for the current conveyance fee before closing, because the amount depends on the county levy. The seller bears the fee and signs the deed before a notary.

How does Ohio define the value on a Massillon conveyance statement?

For a sale, value under Ohio Revised Code 319.202 is the full consideration, counting any mortgage or vendor's lien on the property. A gift, whole or partial, is valued at the open-market price a willing buyer would pay a willing seller.

The statute bars anyone from willfully falsifying the value of the property conveyed. The statement must also address two questions: a tax reduction under section 323.152, and any use of the farm-use valuation program in the previous or current year.

If the answer to either question is yes, the grantor and grantee must sign a sworn instrument setting out the estimated amounts, so ask the seller early whether any reduction applies.

When does a cash sale make sense in Massillon?

A cash sale fits an owner who cannot fund the repairs a house needs, or a family closing out an estate. It also fits sellers who have received a code notice and would rather hand over the house than manage repairs.

Stark County says a penalty of up to $150 may be assessed against the property. The filing is due within 60 days after a conveyance form is filed with the auditor.

Can I get more time to pay taxes on a storm-damaged Massillon house?

How did North Olmsted develop?

The land was part of the Connecticut Western Reserve and was bought by sea captain Aaron Olmsted in 1805 for $30,000, along with the area that is now Olmsted Falls and Olmsted Township.   • Each year the Building Division inspects the exteriors of all residential properties in one ward. Ward 4 was slated to begin in spring 2026.

In Cuyahoga County one Fiscal Office now does the jobs of the old Auditor, Recorder and Engineer. A transfer cannot go through Real Estate Services without either DTE 100, a statement of value and receipt, or DTE 100-EX, which gives the reason a conveyance fee does not apply.

The county describes a single filing without a fee, requires updates within 60 days, and says a $50 penalty may follow each tax bill when the information is missing. Owners who live out of state must name an agent in Ohio.

The county filing sits alongside North Olmsted's own registration, and the county says it applies even to owners the city already has on file. Ask whether both are current so the next owner begins with a clean record.

A direct sale suits some owners: those with a house that needs work, a wish to avoid showings, or an estate on a short clock. Because the city inspects one ward a year, a house with exterior violations may be simpler to sell as it stands than to fix on the city's schedule.

How do the land and the older homes in Bowling Green affect a sale?

The city says a registration stays valid until the owner, the use, or the contact information changes. That makes a sale a reportable event. An owner who lives more than 35 miles away must name a local agent who can accept service around the clock.

Foreclosure runs through Wood County's courts and sheriff. The 2025 county report lists 122 bank foreclosures and 36 sheriff foreclosure property sales. A homeowner who has received a foreclosure notice should ask the lender for a written payoff figure and talk to a title company about how a sale would close out the loan.

  • Photograph the repairs the house needs before you gather offers.
  • Compare each offer's closing costs line by line.

The county's 2025 report mentions a new Bowling Green High School among the projects its building inspectors worked on. Private options include Bowling Green Christian Academy, the Montessori School of Bowling Green, and St. Aloysius.

Lubrizol operates a soap and surfactant plant that opened in 1994 and grew in 2013. The Black Swamp Arts Festival takes place on the first full weekend after Labor Day. The city sits about 20 miles southwest of Toledo and was named the county seat in 1868, replacing Perrysburg. Wikipedia also notes Ohio's first utility-sized wind farm along U.S. Route 6, west of the city.

Who pays the transfer fee on a Wood County sale?

The seller does, under Revised Code 319.202. Once the buyer files a statement of value, the auditor stamps the deed. The settlement sheet from the title company lists the amount.

May I sell a Bowling Green house while a tenant lives in it?

Yes. Investors often like a house with income in place. Hand over the lease, the deposit records, and the city's rental registration and inspection history.

Use the Board of Revision, which takes complaints through the Auditor's office. State law gives you until March 31 of the next tax year, or a later first-half collection close. Call 419-354-9150 for the form.

How did North Royalton develop into the city it is today?

North Royalton is a suburb in southern Cuyahoga County with 31,322 residents at the 2020 census. The community dates to 1818, and an early settler named the township for his native Royalton, Vermont. The name changed to North Royalton sometime between 1880 and 1890 because another Ohio town already used Royalton. It incorporated as a village on April 4, 1927 and became a city in 1961.

The city covers 21.32 square miles. Parma lies to the north, Broadview Heights to the east, Hinckley to the south and Strongsville to the west. Growth was fast after the war: 3,939 people in 1950, 9,290 in 1960 and 23,197 in 1990. The count has barely moved since 2010, rising from 30,444 to 31,322 by 2020, and the federal estimate for mid-2025 is 30,936.

Because the count has stayed nearly level since 2010, your house competes mainly with other established homes in a mature suburb.

What must North Royalton landlords and short-term hosts do?

If the house is a rental, Chapter 1485 of the North Royalton codified ordinances requires a Certificate of Rental Registration from the Building Commissioner before anyone occupies it. The certificate is due by December 31 of the year before it applies, or within thirty days after the house first becomes a rental, and it cannot run past December 31 of the year it was issued. Multi-unit owners must renew every year or file an exemption form.

Timing sets the fee. A single-family rental registered by February 1 pays $50, and one filed after March 1 pays $125. An exemption form costs nothing before February 1 and $50 afterward. Skipping registration is a first-degree misdemeanor under the chapter.

Short-term rentals face tight limits. The chapter defines a short-term rental as any stay under thirty consecutive days. Tenant-occupied units cannot host transient guests at all. Owner-occupants may host for at most fourteen days a year, must live in the home at least 351 days a year, and need a transient rental registration certificate. State law adds a step when a rental changes hands: the county endorses the deed with a reminder that the new owner of residential rental property must file owner information with the auditor under Ohio Revised Code 5323.02.

How is a North Royalton sale recorded at the county?

Each transfer passes through the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Officer's Transfer and Recording division, which merged the former auditor, recorder and engineer roles. Since October 24, 2024 the standard recording fee has been $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each additional page, following Ohio Senate Bill 94. The division works from the fourth floor at 2079 E. Ninth Street in Cleveland, and weekday recording stops at 4 p.m. Staff cannot give legal advice, and the county notes that deed preparation counts as the practice of law, so a closing agent or lawyer should draft the deed.

Inherited houses take special routes. The county's conveyance standards describe an affidavit of real estate inherited under Ohio Revised Code 317.22, a probate court certificate of transfer, and a survivorship affidavit under 5302.17. A separate Great Estates Program page is aimed at families settling an estate.

Separately, section 5302.30 of the Ohio code has sellers give buyers a property disclosure form promptly, with exemptions that include transfers by an estate fiduciary.

When do Cuyahoga County tax bills fall due for a North Royalton seller?

County real estate bills run a year behind, so what is payable in one calendar year covers the year before. The Treasurer's 2026 calendar set the first-half due date at February 19 and the second-half date at August 13. A 10 percent penalty then attached to unpaid first-half bills on March 2 and to unpaid second-half bills on August 23. On September 1, 9 percent interest began on delinquencies from earlier years, with 3 percent more on December 1.

At closing, the settlement agent splits the current bill between you and the buyer and pays any delinquency out of your proceeds. If the valuation looks too high, the county Board of Revision takes complaints each year until March 31, and sale papers such as a closing statement or the DTE 100 count as evidence. The board adds that it may raise a value when the evidence points that way.

More questions about North Royalton, OH

Does a rented North Royalton house need a certificate?

Yes, if the house is a rental. Chapter 1485 bars anyone from occupying a residential rental unit unless a current Certificate of Rental Registration has been issued, and the certificate expires each December 31. Keep it current while tenants live there.

Where is a North Royalton deed filed?

At the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Officer's Transfer and Recording division, with a DTE 100 or DTE 100-EX attached. Recording costs $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each page beyond that.

Are nightly rentals allowed in North Royalton?

Only in narrow cases. Owners living in the home 351 or more days a year may host guests up to fourteen days annually with a registration certificate. Tenant-occupied units may not host them.

When does a Cuyahoga County tax penalty start?

Ten percent is added to an unpaid half-year bill. In 2026 that happened on March 2 for the first half and August 23 for the second.

What if I inherited the North Royalton house?

Title reaches the heirs through a probate court certificate or an affidavit of real estate inherited, and the county lists both routes in its conveyance standards. An heir who did not live in the house within the past year is generally excused from the Ohio disclosure form, but should confirm with a closing agent.

NOAA's 1991 to 2020 normals give Marysville 40.48 inches of precipitation and 24.0 inches of snow a year. Precipitation of at least 0.01 inch falls on about 126 days a year.

January lows average 20.6 degrees Fahrenheit, and the all-time record high is 109. Roofs, gutters, basements and furnaces take that range every year, so inspectors in Union County tend to look at them first.

If any of those items are near the end of their life, say so up front. A cash buyer will price the work, and a financed buyer will bring it up at inspection.

Which Marysville landmarks and neighborhoods shape a sale?

Samuel W. Culbertson laid out Marysville in 1819 beside Mill Creek and named it for his daughter Mary. The village incorporated in 1840, and in 2008 the city was designated a Preserve America Community.

The Union County Courthouse, built in 1883, still serves the county, and the Uptown square around it holds the library, the Scotts museum and city offices. Memorial Hospital of Union County arrived in the medical district in 1952, and the Union County Airport on the east side opened in 1967.

Timberview, an upscale section with a golf course, and Greenwood Colony both sit on the south side. Eljer and Lewis parks have lighted tennis courts, and the Marysville Journal-Tribune, dating to 1849, covers local sales and civic news.

Which school district serves a Marysville house?

Almost all of Marysville falls in the Marysville Exempted Village School District, with a few parcels reaching into Fairbanks Local. The district changes your tax bill, so verify it for the parcel.

The Union County auditor's GIS map includes a school district layer, and the auditor's FAQ explains one wrinkle: if a district line cuts through a house, the district holding the master bedroom taxes the entire house.

The auditor's parcel page has a "Where your taxes go" link that lists every levy and a Total Effective Rate.

What must a Marysville seller disclose?

Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 sets the disclosure duty for houses with up to four units. The seller completes the state form, signs and dates it, and hands it to prospective buyers. It asks about water supply, sewage, roof and foundation, radon, lead paint, asbestos and other known defects.

The duty does not reach every transfer. Excluded sales include:

  • Court-ordered transfers and fiduciary transfers for an estate or trust.
  • Transfers to a spouse or direct-line relatives.
  • Heirs who never lived in the house during the previous year.

A buyer handed the form late may cancel in writing for three business days after receiving it. That right lapses 30 days after acceptance or at closing, if sooner.

What happens at the Union County auditor and recorder?

Ohio Revised Code 5301.01 has the seller sign the deed and acknowledge it before a notary or similar officer. The deed then goes to the Union County Auditor at 233 W. Sixth St. in Marysville, where the buyer's side files a value statement (DTE 100) or an exemption statement (DTE 100EX).

The seller settles the conveyance fee, so ask the auditor which rate applies before closing day. Mailed conveyances reach the recorder only with the auditor's stamp already applied, and the recorder's posted charge for a deed is $39.00 through page two, then $8.00 a page.

When are Union County complaints and exemption notices due?

A Board of Revision complaint on a Union County parcel must reach the auditor after January 1 and on or before March 31. Other posted dates and amounts appear in the table.

Union County items for Marysville owners
ItemWhat the county prints
Board of Revision complaintReceived after January 1 and on or before March 31
Appeal of a board decisionThirty days from the decision letter, filed with the Board of Tax Appeals (DTE Form 4) or Common Pleas Court
Homestead exemption, change in statusNotify the auditor by the first Monday in June
Refund after a value cutDecisions wait 30 days, then adjustments follow in about sixty days
Deed recording$39.00 first two pages, $8.00 each added page

Source: Union County Auditor FAQ and Union County Recorder fee schedule.

  • The 2.5 percent rollback covers owner-occupied homes, one property per owner, and requires an application.
  • A requested change above $50,000 of market value, or $17,500 assessed, sends notice to the school board.
  • After a recent sale, attach the closing statement, contract and deed to support your complaint.

Do Marysville improvements need permits before a sale?

Marysville requires a zoning permit for most additions: decks, fences, swimming pools, sheds, garages and room additions, plus public sidewalks and driveway approaches built by a contractor licensed with the city. Some jobs also need a building permit from the Union County Building Department.

Ask the city zoning office about any structure on your lot that lacks one. Old decks and sheds show up on inspections, and a cash buyer will price in whatever cleanup remains.

Who should consider a cash sale in Marysville?

It suits owners who value a quick, certain close over the last few thousand dollars of price. Common cases:

  • An inherited house nobody plans to occupy.
  • An aging roof, furnace or foundation.
  • Tenants who make showings hard to schedule.
  • A job move on a fixed date.

Set any offer beside what a listing would leave you after repair bills, commission and months of upkeep.

More questions about Marysville, OH

Can I sell a Marysville house without making repairs?

Yes. Ohio sets no repair requirement for a sale, but problems you know about belong on the disclosure form. A cash purchaser accepts the house as found, while a buyer with a lender may ask for fixes.

Who pays the conveyance fee on a Marysville sale?

The seller does. Under Ohio Revised Code 319.202 the grantor settles it before the auditor endorses the deed.

When can I challenge my Marysville property value?

Union County takes these complaints from January 1 to March 31, for the current tax year only. A notarized complaint goes to the auditor by email, fax or mail.

Does an inherited Marysville house need the disclosure form?

Frequently not. Transfers by an estate's fiduciary are excluded, as are sales by heirs who never occupied the house in the previous year.

How do I find the tax rate for a Marysville parcel?

Look up the parcel on the Union County auditor's website. The Total Effective Rate column under "Where your taxes go" gives the rate for that district.

What should a Garfield Heights seller know first?

Garfield Heights puts an inspection between the contract and the closing table. Sellers apply to the Building Department for a Certificate of Inspection, and the city issues a Compliance Certificate that the buyer needs for title transfer.

The city sits in Cuyahoga County, borders Cleveland, spans 7.23 square miles of land, and uses ZIP codes 44105, 44125 and 44128. It began as the Village of South Newburgh in 1907, became Garfield Heights Village in 1919, and was incorporated as a city in 1930 when the population hit 5,000. The name comes from Garfield Park. It runs on a mayor-council system with seven wards under a charter dating to 1956.

Below: the inspection steps, the county filing, and neighborhood facts that bear on price.

How does the Garfield Heights point-of-sale inspection work?

Chapter 1313 of the codified ordinances applies before any sale, transfer or agreement to sell. The buyer must be shown a Certificate of Inspection, or a Certificate of Compliance dated within a year before the agreement.

The city's inspection page and the ordinance set out the steps:

  • The owner or an agent applies on the Building Commissioner's form, and the inspection happens within ten days after the application and fee are received.
  • The certificate follows within ten working days after the inspector gains access and lists code violations found, which the owner must correct within 90 days unless the commissioner extends the time for good cause.
  • The fee is $200 for a dwelling and $300 for a commercial building. Each re-inspection after the first two costs $35, and a missed appointment without one business day of notice costs $25.
  • The buyer signs an acknowledgment of receiving the certificate, and a copy goes to the Building Department as a condition of transferring title.
  • If violations remain at closing, escrow of at least $100 and equal to 110 percent of the higher of two written repair estimates is required, or an approved bond.

The ordinance does not apply to a transfer by inheritance or gift where no real sale is intended. Escrow agents may not transfer title or release funds until the chapter has been satisfied, so file the application early, before an offer is in hand.

What documents does a Garfield Heights buyer have to sign?

The city's page lists a notarized Buyer's Acknowledgement Form, which has to be returned in original to the office. A business buyer must designate an agent, and an out-of-state business must register with the Ohio Secretary of State as a foreign corporation before the Compliance Certificate is issued.

If the buyer is assuming outstanding violations, a notarized Affidavit is also needed, and the buyer has 90 days from the transfer date to finish the repairs. The seller's signature on the affidavit is not required for bank-owned, Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac properties. The page offers separate forms for individuals and businesses, a consent form for an interior inspection, and a snow-covered-property agreement.

The Building and Housing office is at 5407 Turney Road, 2nd floor, open weekdays until 3:45 p.m., and accepts applications by email at buildingdept@garfieldhts.org or by fax. The city says emails are processed within two business days, and fees increased in 2025.

How do Cuyahoga County recording and transfer work for a Garfield Heights sale?

In Cuyahoga County one Fiscal Office division took over what the auditor, recorder and engineer used to do, at 2079 E. Ninth Street, 4th floor, Cleveland. Each transfer must carry a DTE 100 value statement or a DTE 100-EX exemption statement.

The division's page lists the standard recording fee as $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each additional page, effective October 24, 2024 under Senate Bill 94. The office keeps weekday hours, closes recording at 4:00 p.m., and answers at 216-443-2060. Ask the Fiscal Office for the conveyance fee that applies to your sale.

The division notes that drafting a deed is the practice of law under Ohio Supreme Court rulings, so county staff will not advise you. Owners may draft their own, and the signature has to be acknowledged before a notary or similar officer (ORC 5301.01).

How affordable is housing in Garfield Heights by Census data?

Home values here are low by regional standards, with the median owned home valued under $110,000, and the population has slipped since the 2020 Census.

The Census Bureau's estimate base shows a drop of 3.4 percent from April 2020 to July 2025. The 2020 Census reported 13,179 housing units, 9.1 percent of them vacant, with a homeowner vacancy rate of 2.3 percent and a rental vacancy rate of 8.0 percent.

What do buyers see around Garfield Heights?

Wikipedia names Polish, Slovene, German, Italian, Irish and African American communities among the city's ethnic groups. The 2020 density was about 4,119 residents per square mile. The same Census counted 11,985 households, 32.6 percent of them people living alone, and a median age of 38.7. Wikipedia's language breakdown lists English at 93.4 percent and Polish at 2.8 percent.

Parks and amenities that buyers ask about include the Dan Kostel Recreation Center on Turney Road, with an outdoor summer pool and an indoor ice rink, and the Garfield Park Reservation, part of Cleveland Metroparks, in the northeast corner on the Cleveland border. The Wargo Farms parcel, about 45 acres, was sold to Cleveland Metroparks in 2023 for green space and trails.

The Garfield Heights school system runs three elementary schools, one middle school and Garfield Heights High School under a five-member elected board. Catholic options in the city include St. Benedict and Trinity High School. For jobs, the Highland Park development, once City View Center and built on a former landfill, was bought out of receivership in 2020 and has added companies such as MPAC Switchback, MTech, Innoplast and Thermoprene.

How can a Garfield Heights owner sell quickly despite the inspection rule?

Because of the inspection rule, speed depends on who handles the violations.

  • Agent listing: the buyer sees the certificate up front, and you fix cited items inside 90 days or fund the escrow.
  • Sale as-is to an investor: the buyer can assume violations through the affidavit and finish repairs within 90 days of transfer.
  • Inherited property: a transfer by inheritance or gift without a bona fide sale falls outside the point-of-sale chapter.

The Building and Housing page also links a Cuyahoga County list of homes scheduled for demolition, which requires notice to lien holders first. Ask the department how a long violation list could affect your house.

More questions about Garfield Heights, OH

Does Garfield Heights make sellers get an inspection first?

Yes. Chapter 1313 ties a sale to a Certificate of Inspection, and the buyer then needs a Compliance Certificate to take title. The dwelling fee is $200 under the 2024 ordinance.

What is the deadline to correct cited violations?

Ninety days from the certificate, unless the Building Commissioner extends it for good cause. A buyer who assumes the violations by affidavit gets 90 days from the transfer date.

Can I sell if I cannot pay for repairs before closing?

Yes, with escrow or a bond. The escrow runs at least $100 and equals 110 percent of the higher of two written estimates. A buyer who signs the affidavit can also take the house with violations open.

Which office files the deed after a Garfield Heights closing?

The Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office, in its Transfer and Recording division at 2079 E. Ninth Street. The deed travels with a DTE 100 or DTE 100-EX, and recording starts at $39 for two pages.

Does an inherited Garfield Heights house skip the inspection?

Only when it passes by inheritance or gift with no real sale intended. Listing the inherited house for sale brings the chapter back into play, so call the Building Department first.

What makes selling a house in Shaker Heights different from other Ohio suburbs?

Shaker Heights is a planned inner-ring suburb on Cleveland's eastern edge, and a sale here starts with a city inspection that most Ohio towns do not require. The Point of Sale rule covers every residential sale, so the timeline for a fast sale depends on how soon the inspection can be booked.

The Van Sweringen brothers bought the land in 1905, on ground once held by the North Union Shaker settlement that began in 1822. Wikipedia says the community was incorporated in 1912, became a city in 1931 and has roughly 75 percent of its area inside the Shaker Village Historic District, a federal historic listing. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 28,466 people, a 3.4% drop from the April 2020 base, spread over 6.29 square miles of land.

That compact layout means houses sit close together, many were built in the first half of the twentieth century, and the city holds them to its own maintenance chapters in the codified ordinances, Chapter 1411 for residential occupancy and Chapter 1412 for landscaping and yard upkeep.

What is the Point of Sale inspection and who pays for it?

It is a visual interior and exterior inspection the seller must schedule through the city before signing a contract with a buyer, and the seller pays the fee. The city page says the application goes in online through its CitizenServe system, with payment taken in the same step.

An inspector walks the house, the garage and the yard. For a single or two family home the city says the visit takes about 90 minutes. The city asks sellers to allow at least two weeks from application, and three to four weeks in the busy spring season, so applying before you list is the practical move.

  • Single-family home: $200
  • Two-family home: $300
  • Condominium: $150
  • Apartment building: $200 for the first unit and $50 for each additional unit

The Building and Housing Department is at 3400 Lee Road, phone 216-491-1460, with in-person counter service weekdays between 8:30 and 3:30 and phone or email contact until 5 p.m. Permit, license and Point of Sale applications are online only.

What happens if the inspector finds violations?

You get a Certificate of Inspection listing what must be fixed, and you have 90 days to correct the items and book a re-inspection whether or not the house sells. A house with no violations receives a Certificate of Compliance instead, and the city says the property can transfer within 24 months of that first inspection.

If repairs will still be open at closing, the buyer or seller submits an itemized estimate prepared by a registered contractor. The buyer then funds an escrow account at 150 percent of the estimated repair cost, held by the city. The city also reviews requests to swap the escrow for a purchase rehab loan when the buyer will live in the home, and it names the HUD 203(K) program as one example of such a loan.

  • The city grants extensions of the 90-day period when repairs are progressing but unfinished, especially where weather is a factor.
  • A buyer who takes a property at sheriff's sale or another court-ordered auction has 30 days after transfer to obtain the inspection.
  • Violations you dispute or do not understand can be raised with the department; its inspection page lists questions on deadlines, extensions and affordability.

Which other city inspections touch a Shaker Heights house?

Beyond the sale inspection, the city runs a standing cycle. Owner-occupied homes receive an exterior review every five years, and rental properties get an interior and exterior inspection every three years. Neighbor complaints trigger their own inspection, and any violation notice carries a compliance deadline.

For a seller, this means an older violation notice may already be on file. Ask the Building and Housing Department whether anything is open on your address before you sign a listing agreement or accept an offer.

How do Shaker Heights neighborhoods, schools and transit affect a sale?

Buyers here shop by neighborhood, and Wikipedia lists nine of them, each named after one of the original elementary schools: Boulevard, Fernway, Lomond, Ludlow, Malvern, Mercer, Moreland, Onaway and Sussex. Mercer is the largest, and Ludlow is the smallest, and half of it lies in Cleveland but inside the Shaker school district.

Public school students attend the Shaker Heights City School District, which Wikipedia describes as a K-12 district with eight schools and about 5,600 students. Two Greater Cleveland Regional Transit Authority rail lines end in the city: the Blue Line runs down the median of Van Aken Boulevard and the Green Line down the median of Shaker Boulevard. Houses within walking range of a station and a neighborhood school often draw the most interest, so mention both in a listing.

QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 puts typical home value at $303,200, with 60.3% of households owning and 12,806 households in all. Rent at the midpoint is $1,168 a month. Adults with a four-year degree or more make up 69.3% of residents aged 25 and over.

How are property taxes handled when a Shaker Heights house sells?

Cuyahoga County bills the tax, and the Fiscal Office handles valuation and the Homestead program. The county said the second-half 2025 bills were due August 13, 2026, later than usual because of a state law change. Ask the Cuyahoga County Treasurer for the schedule on your parcel so the title company can prorate the bill to the closing date.

The Homestead exemption, according to the Fiscal Office, is open to owners aged 65 and up, those permanently and totally disabled, and certain surviving spouses, with an income limit of $41,000 for the current application and $29,000 of value exempted. The applicant must own and occupy the home on January 1, and the filing deadline is December 31. If the owner sells, the exemption stays with the house for that tax year, but a recipient who buys another home must file again.

Where do you go for each step of a Shaker Heights sale?

Two offices carry most of the work: the city for the inspection and the county for taxes. Start with the city, because the inspection controls the contract date. The table lists the fees the city charges.

Point of Sale fees charged by the City of Shaker Heights, by property type
Property typeFeeSource page
Single-family home$200City Point of Sale Procedure
Two-family home$300City Point of Sale Procedure
Condominium$150City Point of Sale Procedure
Apartment building$200 first unit, $50 each added unitCity Point of Sale Procedure

Taxes and the Homestead program run through the county Fiscal Office at 2079 East Ninth Street in Cleveland, and homestead questions go to 216-443-7420, option 5.

When does a cash offer make sense for a Shaker Heights house?

A cash offer makes sense when a house carries open violations that you do not want to repair before closing. The city allows the buyer to take on all or part of the repair responsibility, so a direct buyer can purchase as-is and set up the escrow for the remaining items.

That arrangement still runs through the city. The inspection must be applied for before the contract is signed, the escrow still equals 150 percent of the contractor estimate, and the buyer holds the repair duty after title passes. Compare at least two offers, ask who covers the inspection fee and escrow, and get the closing date in writing before you sign.

More questions about Shaker Heights, OH

Do I need an inspection to sell my house in Shaker Heights?

Yes. The city requires a Point of Sale inspection for residential sales, and the application must be filed before you enter into a contract with a buyer. The fee is $200 for a single-family home.

How long does a Shaker Heights Point of Sale inspection take to schedule?

Plan on at least two weeks from the application date, and three to four weeks in the spring season, according to the city. The visit itself takes about 90 minutes for a single or two family home.

What is the difference between a Certificate of Compliance and a Certificate of Inspection?

A Certificate of Compliance means the house passed and can transfer within 24 months. A Certificate of Inspection means violations were found and must be fixed within 90 days, even if the house is not sold.

Can a buyer take a Shaker Heights house with violations still open?

Yes, with an itemized contractor estimate and an escrow account for 150 percent of the repair cost. For owner-occupant buyers, the city may accept a purchase rehab loan in place of the escrow.

Who do I ask about property tax on a Shaker Heights sale?

Ask the Cuyahoga County Treasurer and Fiscal Office. They can confirm the due dates on your parcel and any Homestead credit, so the title company prorates the bill correctly at closing.

Kent at a glance

Should a Kent owner list, sell alone or take cash?

A Kent seller has three routes: hire a listing agent, run the sale personally, or sell to a company that closes with its own money and no mortgage underwriting. The choice turns on the house itself, any tenants and your calendar.

  • Listing agent: works for a clean, updated house when weeks of showings and a loan approval are acceptable.
  • Owner run sale: saves the commission, though you price the house, schedule tours, hand over the state disclosure form and chase the deed paperwork.
  • Cash buyer: fits a worn house, a rental with a lease running, an inherited property or a hard closing date.

Just 40.8 percent of Kent households own the roof over their heads, the smallest share among Kent, Kettering, Lakewood and Lancaster. Much of what trades hands near campus is former student housing or small rentals, so buyers raise leases, inspections and licenses early.

How did Kent's housing market take shape?

Kent began as the mill village of Franklin Mills, settled in November 1805 by John and Sally Haymaker beside the Cuyahoga River. The Pennsylvania and Ohio Canal reached it in the 1830s and 1840s, and the Atlantic and Great Western Railroad put its repair shops there in 1864. The village took Marvin Kent's name that year and was incorporated on May 6, 1867.

Two things then reshaped the housing stock. The railroad shops closed in 1930, and Kent State, which began as a teacher training school in 1910, grew until the city went from 12,418 residents in 1950 to 28,183 in 1970. Haymaker Parkway, finished in 1975, eased traffic and blocked rail crossings downtown. Since 2008, public and private spending of about $110 million has gone into downtown projects such as Acorn Alley, a hotel and the Kent Central Gateway transit garage.

The result is a compact city of 9.22 square miles of land, about 3,060 people per square mile, with older frame houses near downtown and campus and postwar blocks farther out.

How do Kent's housing numbers compare with Lancaster's?

Federal estimates put Kent at 27,737 people in mid 2025, a 1.6 percent drop from the April 2020 base. The housing rows below are survey averages for 2020 through 2024.

Kent homes carry a higher median value than Lancaster's while household income runs far lower, a split the student population explains. The same QuickFacts page shows 27.1 percent of Kent residents under the poverty line, and 47.1 percent of Kent adults hold a bachelor's degree.

How do the university, roads and weather affect a Kent sale?

Kent State University employs more people than anyone else here, and its 866 acre main campus on the southeast side shapes demand for houses within walking distance. Davey Tree Expert Company keeps its headquarters in the city and leads the private employers. Educational, health and social services account for 28.4 percent of the local workforce.

  • Schools: the Kent City School District covers most addresses, with four neighborhood elementary schools, Stanton Middle School and Theodore Roosevelt High School. The part of Kent south of State Route 261 belongs to the Field Local School District, so check which one serves a house before you advertise it.
  • Getting around: State Route 59 follows Main Street across downtown, State Route 43 carries traffic north and south, and Interstate 76 is about 3 miles south by way of exit 33. The PARTA bus system links Kent with Akron and Cleveland.
  • Distance: Akron is about 10 miles southwest and Cleveland about 30 miles northwest, so some buyers commute outward.

Kent sits in the secondary snowbelt, with about 36 inches of precipitation a year and thaws above 50 degrees in January and February. Check roofs, gutters and wet basements before listing, and receipts for any repairs are worth keeping with the disclosure form.

Which Kent offices should a seller contact before closing?

Start with the Building Division at 930 Overholt Road, phone 330-678-8107, which handles permits and the city's Exterior Maintenance Code. Ask whether any permit on your address was never closed out, because unfinished work can hold up a closing.

  • Rentals with four or more unrelated tenants: the Kent City Health Department, at 201 E. Erie Street, second floor, phone 330-678-8109, licenses these multiple use dwellings and investigates housing maintenance complaints under the city's Environmental Health and Housing Maintenance Code.
  • One and two family rentals: these are licensed through the Community Development Department, which can be reached at 330-678-8108. For code issues at unlicensed homes and small rentals, the city lists 330-678-8464.
  • Zoning: new construction, additions, accessory structures and signs need a zoning permit before work starts.

With tenants in place, tell the buyer which license applies and keep a copy for the closing file.

How does the deed transfer work in Portage County?

Portage County's Auditor runs the transfer step for Kent, a city that is the county's largest. The Auditor's Real Estate Department handles each deed ahead of recording. The Auditor's page prints the fee as $4.00 per $1,000.00 of the purchase price plus 50 cents per parcel, and it links the DTE 100 form.

Ohio Revised Code 319.202 has the buyer's side submit the statement of value, while the grantor pays the fee. The statement also asks whether the parcel gets a property tax reduction or farm use valuation, so know your answer before closing day. Parcel histories, valuations and sales data can be searched on the Auditor's site.

Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 asks owners of homes with one to four units to give each buyer a signed disclosure form. Transfers by an estate fiduciary, and a sale to someone who has already occupied the home for twelve months, appear among the exceptions. A buyer who never gets the form can back out, within a window that ends no later than closing.

Is a cash buyer a good fit for a worn or tenant occupied Kent house?

Cash is worth a look when certainty outranks the top price. Kent examples include a rental whose lease has months left, repairs that would stall a lender's appraisal, or a vacant house left behind by an estate.

Get any offer on paper, with the closing date, the party paying title and recording costs, and the buyer's rule if a walkthrough finds something new. Set two or three offers beside the net an agent would deliver after commission and repairs, and ask the Portage County Auditor what conveyance charge applies so the settlement sheet holds no surprises.

More questions about Kent, OH

Can I sell a Kent house with student tenants still inside?

Yes. Read the lease for its end date, then either sell to a buyer who takes over the tenancy or plan the closing around move out. Confirm which Kent license covers the rental and hand the buyer copies of the lease and license.

Who collects the transfer fee when a house sells in Kent?

The Portage County Auditor collects it, and the city does not. The Auditor's page lists $4.00 per $1,000.00 of the purchase price plus 50 cents per parcel, and Ohio Revised Code 319.202 places the fee on the grantor.

Does selling my Kent home as is skip the disclosure form?

Usually no. Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 reaches one to four unit residential property, and a discounted as is price leaves the duty to complete the form in good faith untouched. Estate fiduciary sales and the other listed transfers are exempt.

Which school district does my Kent house belong to?

Most of Kent is in the Kent City School District, but addresses south of State Route 261 are in the Field Local School District. Ask the district or the county before you put a district name in a listing.

How can I find out what my Kent house is worth?

Search the parcel on the Portage County Auditor's property records for valuation and sales history, then compare an agent's opinion with written cash offers. The county figure serves tax purposes and often differs from a market price.

What is the Green, Ohio housing market like?

Green lies in the southeast corner of Summit County, between Akron and Canton, and covers an unusually wide area for a suburb at 32.03 square miles of land plus 1.5 square miles of water. That makes for a spread-out market of subdivisions, lakeside lots and former farm parcels rather than a compact grid.

Green Township was created in 1809 as part of Stark County and joined Summit County when that county formed in 1840. Hamlets such as Greensburg dotted the township, farms gave way to developers after 1950, and voters approved merging the village with the rest of the township in 1991. Green was a collection of farms, hamlets and coal-bearing land by 1900, and the local economy then shifted toward business and manufacturing. The city's motto, "A township from the past, a city of the future," reflects that history.

Green uses ZIP codes 44232, 44312, 44319, 44685 and 44216, and some of those addresses are shared with neighboring places. Ask the Summit County Fiscal Office to confirm that your parcel is inside the city limits before you rely on city rules.

How much does a typical Green home cost, by Census data?

Green skews toward owners: 75.1 percent of households own, the middle owned home is valued at $280,200, and the middle household earns $95,047.

QuickFacts adds that 89.7 percent of residents were in the same house a year before, 42.4 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree, 93.9 percent of households have broadband, and the average commute is 23.7 minutes. Retail sales in 2022 came to $1,355,338,000, about $49,708 per resident.

The business rows give 2022 receipts of $492,696,000 for transportation and warehousing, $265,218,000 for health care and social assistance, and $100,627,000 for lodging and food service. The city counts 1,093 veterans, and 3.0 percent of residents were born abroad.

How fast has Green grown, and who lives in its homes?

Green added residents at every count: 22,817 in 2000, 25,699 in 2010 and 27,475 in 2020, with the 2025 estimate at 27,553. Density rose from about 801.7 people per square mile in 2010 to 857.7 in 2020, a far lower density than Garfield Heights or Gahanna.

In 2020 the Census found 11,195 households. Married couples headed 53.8 percent, children under 18 lived in 29.7 percent, and 26.7 percent were one-person households, including 12.6 percent where that person was 65 or older.

Green sits at about 1,198 feet of elevation within the Akron metropolitan area. A listing should name the city and the school district, Green Local Schools, since many Green addresses carry Akron-area ZIP codes.

What are the zoning and code rules in Green?

The city's Zoning Division issues permits, inspects new structures and enforces the City Code, and it also takes right-of-way applications for aprons and road openings. Its Zoning page lists the most common code complaints:

  • High grass
  • Litter, garbage and debris
  • Junk or inoperable vehicles
  • Storage of RVs, campers and boats
  • Property disrepair

Clear any of these before listing. The division is at the Central Administration Building, 1755 Town Park Blvd., and its phone is 330-896-6605. The Land Development Code is in Part Twelve of the city's codified ordinances.

The city page also names the Summit County Department of Building Standards in Akron and Summit County Public Health on West Market Street as permit and inspection agencies.

What does the Summit County Fiscal Office charge to transfer a Green deed?

Summit County's fee page sets the conveyance fee at $4.00 per $1,000 of price, rounded up to the next $100, and adds 50 cents for each lot in the legal description, even on exempt transfers. Hancock and Franklin counties show $3 per $1,000.

On the Property Transfer page, the department takes the DTE 100 statement of value or the DTE 100(EX) exemption form, under ORC 319.202 and 319.54(G)(3). Properly prepared forms must reach the Property Transfer Department by 3:30 p.m. to have the legal description approved the same business day. Under ORC 319.202 the value on the statement is the full consideration, mortgage or lien balances included, the grantor pays the fee, and willfully falsifying the value is prohibited.

The Recording Division is at 175 South Main Street, 4th floor, Akron. An unrecorded deed loses to a later buyer who had no notice of it, which is why ORC 5301.25 sends every deed to the county recorder. The same section adds a drafting rule: when a survey was made of the land being conveyed, the surveyor's name has to appear in the deed, and the county auditor can insist on it. Ask the Recording Division for the current per-page recording charge.

Which employers and amenities draw buyers to Green?

Wikipedia quotes the city's 2022 annual financial report: Green Local School District leads with 632 jobs, then

  • Summa Health System, 555
  • Fannie May Confection, 550
  • FedEx Custom Critical, 495
  • Diebold Nixdorf, 427
  • Target, 369

Interstate 77 serves the city, and the Akron-Canton Regional Airport lies partly inside Green and partly in Jackson Township. Green opened the first two-lane roundabout in Summit County in 2009 and had 11 roundabouts as of 2024.

Boettler Park, a 26-acre park with trails, fishing, picnicking and biking, and the Singer Lake Bog nature preserve are public spaces in the city. Public school students attend Green Local Schools. A mayor and a seven-member council run the city, with four of the council members chosen by ward and everyone limited to two consecutive four-year terms.

What should a Green seller know about pipelines and local history?

Green fought the NEXUS Pipeline in court starting in 2016 because the line runs near residential neighborhoods, wetlands and the Comet Lake Dam. Construction began in 2018 after the city reached a $7.5 million settlement. If your lot is near the route, check your title paperwork for any easement before a buyer asks.

From about 1950 farmers began selling land to developers, so Green houses range from older farm properties to newer subdivision homes.

Which sale routes work for a Green house on a deadline?

  • Agent listing: a fit for move-in-ready homes where recent nearby sales give a clear price.
  • Investor sale: suited to dated houses, open code complaints, or an estate sale on a deadline.
  • Owner sale: saves commission but requires you to prepare the DTE 100 and deed paperwork.
  • Sale to a relative or neighbor: the exemption form may apply, and the 50 cent lot fee is owed either way.

Whichever route you pick, price the house against nearby Green sales, check for open zoning complaints, and pull together the survey and title papers. If the lot has a septic system, ask Summit County Public Health what records it keeps.

Who issues permits for a house in Green?

The city's Zoning Division handles zoning permits and inspections of new structures, and the Summit County Department of Building Standards is listed as the county agency.

How much is the Summit County conveyance fee on a Green sale?

The county's fee page shows $4.00 per $1,000, with the price rounded up to the next $100, plus 50 cents per lot. Forms in by 3:30 p.m. get same-day legal description approval.

In Akron, at the Fiscal Office Recording Division on South Main Street, because Ohio records a deed in the county where the land sits.

Green Local School District leads with 632 jobs in the city's 2022 financial report, ahead of Summa Health System, Fannie May Confection and FedEx Custom Critical.

How do I find out about code complaints on my Green house?

Call the Zoning Division at 330-896-6605. Overgrown grass, junk vehicles, stored RVs and general disrepair top its list of violations.

How can a Troy homeowner sell without months of showings?

Fast options in Troy are an as-is cash purchase or a listing priced to sell, and the right pick follows the house itself. A downtown address inside the Historic District raises different questions than a recent subdivision home, so decide where your property stands first.

  • Agent listing: reaches Dayton-area buyers, with an inspection and loan approval still ahead of closing.
  • Owner-handled sale: you draft the contract, deliver the disclosure form and line up the deed.
  • Direct as-is purchase: the buyer inherits the repairs, and you can set closing to fit your move.

Any route ends the same way: the deed clears the Miami County Engineer and Auditor, then goes to the Recorder.

What is Troy, Ohio like for a seller?

Troy seats Miami County and is its largest city, set on the Great Miami River roughly 19 miles north of Dayton. Surveyors platted it around 1807, and the post office dates to 1824. Troy was among the cities touched by the Great Flood of 1913. The city measures 11.94 square miles, with 11.72 of land.

The older core is distinctive. Overfield Tavern, from 1808, is now a museum, and the Troy-Hayner Cultural Center fills a 1914 Romanesque mansion. The Hobart Welded Steel House Company built just 22 prefabricated steel houses, every one in Troy, and 16 survive on the National Register of Historic Places. The Hobart Institute of Welding Technology opened in 1930, and the Troy Public Square and Miami County Courthouse are also listed.

Troy's Historic District is an overlay running roughly from the Miami River on the north to Canal Street on the south, and from Oxford Street on the west to Clay Street on the east. That footprint matches the city's edge when it became county seat in 1807. The Planning Commission reviews alterations there, so check before you repaint, reside or replace windows for a sale.

What do the Census numbers show for Troy?

Troy is growing. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 27,344 residents, up 3.8 percent from the April 2020 base, and each census from 1990 to 2020 counted more people than the one before.
